comments.species: High-density hippocampal cultures were prepared from newborn mice and infected with lentiviruses as described (Kaeser et al., 2009).
comments.rationale: RIM1/RIM2 double knockout cultures have a reduction in the size of the sucrose pool at inhibitory synapses, demonstrating a role for RIM proteins in vesicle priming (fig 1c). This is mediated by activation of Munc13 through the Zinc finger domain (figures 3,4 5 and 6). Due to the strong homology between RIM1 and RIM2, both proteins are assumed to be redundant in this process. Action potential mediated pool measurements have confirmed a role in priming at the calyx of Held (Han et.al. 2011), and sucrose pool measurements in cultured neurons have confirmed this role at excitatory synapses (Kaeser et.al. 2011).

comments.rationale:
As a motor adapter, FEZ1 functions to link syntaxin-1 to the Kinesin-1 motor. Loss of FEZ1 (UNC-76) in C. elegans led to the abnormal of syntaxin-1 along neurons axons which is different from its usual distribution along axonal plasma membranes. Expression of the FEZ1/UNC-76 phospho-mutant also resulted in the same phenotype.

In a subsequent paper (Butkevich et al., 2016; PMID 27247180), loss of FEZ1 function either in the unc-76 mutant or loss of the activating kinase PAR-1/MARK was further shown to lead to loss of presynaptic specialisations.

These data highlight a role of FEZ1 in establishing presynaptic specialisations via transporting presynaptic components.

comments.rationale:
To study synaptic plasticity, the authors correlated pre- and postsynaptic activation using a train of stimuli (16s, 5 Hz) delivered to one Schaffer collateral/commissural input that was paired with a postsynaptic injection of a spike-inducing depolarizing current. Two conditions were studied: (1) when the onset of EPSPs was about 20 ms after postsynaptic spiking, the EPSC amplitude of both stimulated (homosynaptic) and non-stimulated (heterosynaptic) inputs showed a persistent reduction following the correlated activation (LTD protocol) and (2) when the onset of EPSPs was about 5 ms before postsynaptic spiking, the EPSC amplitude of the homosynaptic input showed a persistent increase in amplitude whereas the one of the heterosynaptic input was not affected (LTP protocol).

Functional blockade of IP3R1 by postsynaptic loading of a monoclonal antibody against IP3R1 or genetic deletion of IP3R1 using IP3R1-deficient mice impacted both conditions: when studying LTD (1) lacking IP3R1 function led to a conversion of homosynaptic LTD to LTP and eliminated heterosynaptic LTD. When studying LTP (2) a significant enhancement of homosynaptic LTP was observed, resulting in even higher potentiation. Therefore, IP3R1 presents a role in regulating Ca2+ release from internal stores in the postsynaptic neuron, which can control polarity and magnitude of postsynaptic plasticity.

20/2/2017 Pim
-primary paper: Flot1 is required for PKC-triggered internalization and Amphiphysin-induced reverse transport of DA in primary DA neuron. This role at the level of the synapse is not shown.
-SynGO ID #201: Flot1 is localized in synapses of hippocamal neurons. Pre or postsynaptic localization cannot be distinguished based on the presented data.
-Inference: Flot1 regulates "NT reuptake" in the synapse.

8/8/2017 Pim
- On second thought I have agreed for the term 'neurotransmitter reuptake (GO:0098810). Flot1 is shown to mediate PKC-triggered internalization and Amphiphysin-induced reverse transport of DA in primary DA neurons. According to SynGO guidelines this does not have to happen AT the synapse; BPs are included when relevant for synaptic function. Without evidence shown this is implied by the authors "Plasmalemmal neurotransmitter transporters (NTTs) regulate the level of neurotransmitters, such as dopamine (DA) and glutamate, after their release at brain synapses". Another point of doubt is the 're-' part of the term 'reuptake'. No experiments are shown in a synaptic context and secretion from synapses and consecutive re-uptake are not shown in the paper. I have allowed this under an IC evidence type: the justification here is that whatever Dopamine is around cells that this has to be secreted by a synapse at some time.

comments.rationale:
It is shown that postsynaptic perfusion with PKM zeta (a constitutively active splice variant of the PRKCZ gene) increases postsynaptic AMPAR responses. This is inhibited by pep2m, a peptide that inhibits NSF/GluR2 interactions (Figure 1). The effect does not require exocytotic insertion of GluRs, since Botox B is unable to inhibit the effect (Figure 1D), and there is no increase in the surface or total level or GluR2 (Figure 3E). Using synaptosomes, it is shown that PKM-zeta dependent LTP does lead to a increase in synaptic GluR2 and GluR3, and that this is blocked by pep2m and a ZIP (a inhibitor with some specificity to PKM-zeta). It is thus concluded that PKM-zeta increases AMPAR responses by recruiting extrasynaptic GluRs to the PSD.

Ling et.al. 2006 demonstrates that PKM zeta-induced potentiation requires an increase in the number of receptors, not an increase in receptor conductance.

It should be noted that PKM-zeta has long been suspected to be essential for postsynaptic LTP, but that this is subject on an ongoing debate. (Tsokas et.al. 2016).

-PI3K activation leads to increased surface expression of GluRs, which is inhibited by Myr-aPKC-PS (Figure 3C-F).
-PI3K activation leads to increased mEPSC amplitudes, which can be blocked by PKC-lambda shRNA and Myr-aPKC-PS (Figure 3G-H).

It should be noted that at the concentration used, Myr-aPKC-PS also strongly inhibits PKC-zeta (see Figure 1D and Tsokas et al 2016). Thus, in several assays in this publication, it cannot be excluded that observed effects are mediated by PKC-zeta. The role of PKC-lambda in LTP is debated and likely involves an interplay with PKC-zeta expression (Tsokas et al 2016).

A forebrain-specific knockout for calcineurin beta is created (CaNB is encoded by the gene PPP3R1, which is called CNB1 in this paper). This knockout has a strong reduction in LTD, as shown in figure 3. This process has been shown to be dependent on receptor endocytosis (Man et al 2000). 24/11/2017 Pim
- Normally we would not allow annotation against the term 'postsynaptic neurotransmitter receptor endocytosis (GO:0098884)'. The reason is this may lead to very problematic/unintuitive gene-process annotations f.i. presynaptic proteins that affect LTP then also regulate postsynaptic NTR endocytosis. This is an exception to that guideline. There is functional data referenced (PMID:11100150, ticket #254) that shows that calcineurin is involved in NTR endocytosis, but this data does not distinguish between gene paralogs. Together with the data on LTP this makes the annotation against 'postsynaptic neurotransmitter receptor endocytosis (GO:0098884)' a straight-forward inference. This inference across mulitple papers is difficult to capture in a IC pattern. The authors themselves give two possible mechanisms that may underlie the LTP effect:

"Two potential mechanisms by which calcineurin could trigger LTD have emerged from recent studies, both related to regulation of AMPA receptors. First, a recent study showed that LTD and dedepression are associated with the dephosphorylation and phosphorylation, respectively, of a PKA phosphorylation site on the GluR1 subunit of AMPA receptors ... A second possibility, not mutually exclusive with the first, is that calcineurin triggers LTD by stimulating AMPA receptor endocytosis (Beattie et al., 2000; Lin et al., 2000)."

comments.species: Mice carrying floxed alleles of Crk and Crk-L have been described previously (Park et al. 2006; Park and Curran 2008). Mice that carry a myf5cre allele, which confers Cre recombinase expression in myoblasts and myotubes, have been described previously (Tallquist et al. 2000).
comments.rationale: Crk-L is a postsynaptic protein which plays a crucial role in NMJ synapse formation concomitantly with CrkI/II, by directly interacting with Dok-7. Knockdown of both CrkI/II and Crk-L was necessary to induce a significant effect in postsynaptic AChR cluster formation, an effect that was partially rescued by overexpression of CrkL (Hallock et al., 2015). Transgenic mice lacking CrkL and CrkI/II in myotubes show neonatal lethality and study of their embryonic neuromuscular synapses reveal a lower number of synapses which resulted in a low level of innervated myofibers, decreased synaptic size and decreased number of synaptic AChRs. Moreover, motor axons grow beyond AChR cluster. Overall, CrkL has a crucial role in neuromuscular pre- and postsynaptic differentiation and its absence can be compensated by CrkI/II.

comments.rationale:
In this paper, the function of syb1 is investigated in the NMJ in Syb1 lew/lew mutant mice. Authors first checked if Syb1 is involved in synaptic formation. However, they did not find any evidence for this hypothesis.
In the second step, they used electrophysiology to investigate if Syb1 is involved in spontaneous or Ca2+-triggered exocytosis. They found that both spontaneous (Fig. 3) and evoked neurotransmission (Fig. 4) was reduced compared to WT mice. Then they measure the size of the readily releasable pool in Syb1 lew/lew mutant. They did not find any change compared to control. Therefore, they reject the hypothesis that Syb1 is involved in the priming of synaptic vesicles (Fig. 7).
 They found that reduction of neurotransmitter release is due to reduction Ca2+ sensitivity and cooperativity of neuromuscular synaptic transmission in Syb1lew/lew mice (Fig. 8). and elevation of external Ca2+ restores some of the phenotypes such as short-term plasticity (Fig. 9).

Fig 7: Los of KCNQ5 staining after ablation of presynaptic fibers:
In a different set of experiments, we investigated whether KCNQ5 was present in excitatory endings of the auditory nerve. This was observed in rats cochleotomized at 30 days old (Fig. 7G-I). The degree of cochlear nerve disintegration at its entrance to the CN was evaluated in sections labeled with an anti-calretinin antibody. Most calretinin labeling in fibers had disappeared from the neuropil 10 days after cochlear ablation, indicating exten- sive fiber and terminal degeneration in the CN (Illing et al., 1997; Caminos et al., 2005). In sections from cochleoto- mized animals labeled with immunoperoxidase to detect KCNQ5 immunoreactivity, it was seen that auditory nerve fiber degeneration was matched by a dramatic de- crease of KCNQ5-labeled endings around cell bodies and in the neuropil (Fig. 7H,I). Often, KCNQ5 immunoreac- tivity completely disappeared, which was particularly well seen in synaptic endings around cell bodies in the AVCN (Fig. 7I). Therefore, excitatory endings from the auditory nerve in the AVCN are a main source of synaptic endings where KCNQ5 is expressed.

comments.rationale:
Figure 1: Identification of presynaptic KCNQ current:
(a) A slow voltage ramp (13 mV s-1) with a K+-based internal solution evoked an outward current (black) that was strongly inhibited by 10-20 μM XE991, a KCNQ channel blocker (gray). (b) Outward current blocked by the KCNQ channel blocker linopirdine. (c) Outward current potentiated by the KCNQ channel opener flupirtine.

Figure 3: Evidence for the presynaptic KCNQ subunit to be KCNQ5:
Given the very low expression of
KCNQ2-KCNQ4, these results suggest that XE991-sensitive current is generated by channels composed solely of KCNQ5 subunits.
The conclusions based on immunohistochemistry were con- firmed by a pharmacological approach. Recent studies have iden- tified compounds whose effects differ qualitatively among different KCNQ subunits. Presynaptic K+ current was measured under con- ditions in which almost all current is XE991 sensitive (Fig. 1a). Diclofenac is a KCNQ2-KCNQ4 activator but a blocker of KCNQ5 (ref. 26). We found that 100 μM diclofenac inhibited the presyn- apticK+ currentby53±4%at0mV(Fig.3k;P=0.004,n=5). Among cloned KCNQ subunits, UCL2077 is reported to inhibit all but KCNQ5, which exhibits voltage dependent potentiation by the drug27. UCL2077 at 10 μM potentiated K+ current by 8 ± 2% at 0 mV (Fig. 3l; P = 0.05, n = 4). Although it is controversial whether KCNQ1 is present in the CNS28, this subunit does not have a pro- file of sensitivity to diclofenac or UCL2077 resembling that of the presynaptic current26,27. These results support our immunohisto- chemical observations and indicate that the presynaptic KCNQ subunit is likely to be KCNQ5.

The authors reported that VAMP4 is needed for Activity-dependent Bulk endocytosis (ADBE), a pathway involved in the recovery of synaptic vesicles after intense stimulation. To determine whether VAMP4 is involved in bulk endocytosis, the authors inhibited GSK3, a kinase known to be active in ADBE, and found that inhibition of ADBE greatly diminishes the proportion of nerve terminals displaying activity-dependent slow VAMP4-pHluorin downstrokes, suggesting this downstroke reflects bulk endosome acidification.

comments.rationale:
Activity-dependent bulk endocytosis (ADBE) is the dominant SV endocytosis mode under intense neuronal activity.

The authors investigated whether directed sorting of SV cargo occurs at the plasma membrane during ADBE, since this will ultimately impact on the molecular composition of SVs generated via this endocytosis mode.

They examined the retrieval of different SV cargo molecules during intense stimulation using a series of genetically encoded pH-sensitive reporters in neuronal cultures, and they found that only one was preferentially trafficked via ADBE-VAMP4.

Author showed two important results:
1) VAMP4 is not simply represented as an ADBE cargo, actually authors showed by using biochemical fractionation experiments, that endogenous VAMP4 was selectively enriched on bulk endosomes.

2) VAMP4 is essential for ADBE to proceed. Authors determined this by using validated shRNA oligonucleotides against VAMP4. When 40Hz/10s stimulation was applied, VAMP4 knockdown abolished TMR-dextran uptake, an inhibition fully rescued by expression of wild-type VAMP4- pHluorin (Figures 7B and C). Therefore, in addition to being the first identified ADBE cargo molecule, VAMP4 is essential for this key endocytosis mode.

VAMP4 Location: Figure 7A --> Representative images show nerve terminals labeled with VAMP4 antibodies after immunogold detection and silver enhancement. Almost all silver particles were localized to endosomal structures after 40 Hz stimulation (indicated by arrows).

comments.rationale:
An ADCY1 knockout is used to demonstrate that cAMP production by adenylyl cyclase 1 (AC1) is required mossy fiber LTP.

- Knockout of AC1 leads to a strong reduction in cAMP production in hippocampal neurons (figure 1-2).
- Mossy fiber LTP is strongly reduced in the knockout (figure 6).
- Forskolin (an agonist of PKA, the major downstream effector of cAMP) is still able to potentiate synaptic transmission in the knockout (figure 8). This shows that pathways downstream of cAMP production are intact.

Numerous studies have demonstrated that mossy fiber LTP is expressed presynaptically (Zalutsky & Nicoll), and requires cAMP production and the activation of PKA. Since this form of LTP does not induce changes in presynaptic calcium influx (Kamiya et.al 2002), it must operate through potentiation of synaptic vesicle exocytosis.

comments.rationale:
Using a ADCY8 knockout, it is shown that adenylyl cyclase 8 (AC8) is required for mossy fiber LTP.

-AC8 knockout displays a reduction in cAMP production (figure 1).
-Mossy fiber LTP is strongly reduced in the AC8 knockout (figure 4).

Numerous studies have demonstrated that mossy fiber LTP is expressed presynaptically (Zalutsky & Nicoll), and requires cAMP production and the activation of PKA. Since this form of LTP does not induce changes in presynaptic calcium influx (Kamiya et.al 2002), it must operate through potentiation of synaptic vesicle exocytosis.

In addition, it is shown that other forms of plasticity (PTP and PPF) are also affected by AC8 knockout (figure 4). This is in line with a defect in regulation of synaptic vesicle exocytosis. However, based on the available data, it cannot be excluded that other processes (e.g. potentiation of calcium influx) contribute to PTP or PPF at the mossy fiber synapse.

ELKS1 and ELKS2 are both expressed at synapses in these cultures (Held et.al. 2016).

comments.rationale:
Using an ELKS1/2 double knockout, this publication provides multiple lines of evidence that ELKS1 controls synaptic vesicle priming at excitatory synapses.

-ELKS DKO leads to a reduction in spontaneous and action potential-evoked release at excitatory synapses (Figure 2).
-ELKS DKO displays a reduction of sucrose-induced vesicle fusion, an established method for measuring vesicle priming. This effect can be rescued by reintroduction of ELKS1 (figure 7). In addition, there is a significant reduction in vesicle fusion during short action potential trains, which is in line with a defect in priming (figure 4).

13/4/2017 Pim
- Effect on priming may be synapse type related. In inhibitory synapses this effect seems absent although ELKS influences SV release via an indirect mechanism. (see ticket #333).

comments.species: Mice were generated according to standard procedures (Ho et al., 2006 and Kaeser et al., 2008), targeting exon 3 of the ELKS2 gene by homologous recombination in R1 ES cells.
comments.rationale:
Kaeser et.al. provides evidence that ELKS2 is involved in synaptic vesicle priming at inhibitory synapses.

-In hippocampal slices, there is an increase in action potential-evoked release at inhibitory synapses. There is a small effect on release probability (as measured by paired pulse), this is not sufficient to explain the effect on evoked release. This indirectly suggests an increase of the primed vesicle pool (Figure 4).
-More directly, in hippocampal cultures, there is an increase in vesicle priming (measured with sucrose application, figure 7). This preparation shows an similar increase in action-potential evoked release (figure 6).

It should be noted that there is a complex interplay between ELKS1 and ELKS2 in vesicle priming, that is dependent on the type of synapses. In ELKS1/2 double knockouts, there is no effect on vesicle priming in inhibitory synapses (Liu et.al. 2014, Held et.al. 2016), but an decrease at excitatory synapses (Held et.al. 2016). The exact contribution of ELKS2 in vesicle priming has not been determined.

comments.species: Primary mouse hippocampal cultures from newborn pups were generated as previously described (Ho et al., 2006; Kaeser et al., 2008; Kaeser et al., 2009; Kaeser et al., 2011).
comments.rationale:
Liu et.al. provides multiple lines of evidence that ELKS proteins control action potential-evoked calcium influx in inhibitory presynaptic terminals.

-In presynaptic calcium imaging, ELKS DKO shows a reduction in AP-induced calcium entry (Figure 8).
-ELKS DKO displays a reduction in AP-induced vesicle fusion as measured with electrophysiology (Figure 5). Release has a reduced sensitivity to Ca2+ (EC50) without affecting the cooperativity. This is in line with a defect in calcium entry, and not the calcium sensor of the release machinery.
-There is no defect in the synaptic localization of calcium channels, as shown with immunocytochemistry (figure 9).
Taken together, these data show that ELKS proteins control the opening of calcium channels.

Since this study has been performed in ELKS1/2 double knockouts, the exact contribution of ELKS1 or ELKS2 is currently unknown.

13/4/2017 Pim
- Effect on SV release synapse type related. In inhibitory synapses (this annotation) ELKS influences SV release via an indirect mechanism, whereas in excitatory synapses ELKS regulates SV priming (see ticket #331).

comments.rationale:
Gronborg, M et al compared the protein composition of synaptic vesicles enriched either in VGLUT-1 or VGAT by mass spectrometry and validated the data by means of microscopy and immunoblotting. Among the differentially distributed proteins between the two SV subpopulations, MAL2 protein was identified as preferentially enriched in the VGLUT1-containing SV fracton (Fig. 2B and Table 1 - quantitative proteomic comparison of proteins from immunoisolated SVs).
MAL2, predicted to contain four transmembrane domains, was mainly enriched in the VGLUT-1-specific SVs as shown by immunoblotting with newly raised antibody (Fig. 3, Fig 6 C-E): Pronase treatment of synaptic vesicles (Stenius et al.1995) and Triton X-114 extraction (Bordier 1981) helped identifying MAL2 as integral protein in the SVs with its N-terminus exposed in the cytoplasm and not into the vesicular lumen. MAL2 was strongly enriched in subcellular fractionation of whole rat brain similar to synaptophysin, Rab3a, synaptotagmin-1 and VGLUT-2 in the CPG-SV fraction (Fig. 6C). This finding was confirmed by EM immunogold double labeling of MAL2 and VGLUT-1 (Fig. 6D). MAL2 showed preferential expression in brain and liver as surveyed by immunoblotting of rat tissue samples (Fig. 6E).
Finally, double immunofluorescent labeling of MAL2 with either VGLUT-1 or VGAT in primary cultures of hippocampal neurons (Fig. 7) as well as in mouse and rat hippocampal and cerebellar sections (Fig. 8 A-D) confirmed selective but not exclusive presence of MAL2 in glutamatergic neurons. Double immunogold labeling of MAL2 and VGLUT-1 in mossy fiber terminals (rat CA3 area) (Fig. 8E, Fig S4 C-D) indicated vesicular colocalization of both proteins on SVs.

Vesicular aminergic-associated transporter (Slc10a4) is co-localized with synaptic vesicles positive for VAChT and VMAT2 as show by STED microscopy and in situ proximity ligation assay (Fig. 1 F-I). Immunoblotting of purified synaptic vesicles for VAChT, VMAT2 and VAAT confirm VAAT-localization to SVs (Fig. 4 C).
This observation is supported by co-localization analysis of Slc10a4 with VAChT and VMAT2 in mouse striatum and spinal cord, Fig. S1 H-I and S1 J-K, respectively. A biochemical support for these findings is shown in Fig. S1 O (immunoisolation of transporter-positive vesicles followed by Western blot detection).
Additionally, association of the transporter with SVs at symmetrical synapses is assessed by immunogold labelling (electron microscopy, see Fig. S1 L).

Immunohistochemistry experiments on adult mouse brain sections (Fig. S1 B-F) and on human brain samples (Fig. S1 G) confirm distribution of the protein in brain regions containing cholinergic, dopaminergic or serotonergic neurons. The data is supported by RNA in situ hybridization experiments detecting slc10a4 RNA in cholinergic and monoaminergic regions of mouse CNS (Fig 1A-E).

comments.species: Mutant mice were generated by homologous recombination experiments with R1 embryonic stem cells and genotyped as described in SI Materials and Methods.
comments.rationale:
This publication provides evidence that Piccolo is involved in presynaptic vesicle clustering. In neuronal cultures of Piccolo knockout mice, with additional knockdown of Bassoon, there is a reduction in the in the number of vesicles per synaptic bouton (Figure 4G-H). There also appears to be a reduction of the number of docked vesicles (Figure 4L, N), but it unclear whether this is a direct effect, or caused indirectly by a reduction in vesicle clustering. Knockout of Piccolo alone had no effect on vesicle clustering or docking, suggesting that Piccolo and Bassoon may be redundant in this.

The data presented in this paper should be considered with some caution. The genetic manipulation to delete Piccolo is a hypomorph, meaning that some Piccolo splice variants are still expressed (Waites et.al. 2011). In addition, due to the very large size of Piccolo, available techniques make it difficult to accurately measure Piccolo levels in cell lysates. Waites et.al. also shows that Piccolo regulates the assembly of presynaptic F-actin, which is in line with phenotype in vesicle clustering.

comments.rationale:
Using both confocal microscopy and superresolution STED microscopy, is demonstrated that DSyd-1 is present at the presynaptic active zone of the drosophila neuromuscular junction.

DSyd-1 closely colocalized with BRP a well established marker of the active zone (Figure 2D, 3). Dsyd-1 staining was reminiscent of the staining pattern of DLiprin, another constituent of the active zone (Figure 3).

A knockout control is provided for the DSyd-1 antibody.

The mammalian gene mSYD1A might also be present at synapses (Wentzel 2013) but currently available data are not sufficient to prove this.

comments.rationale:
This publication provides multiple lines of evidence that DSyd1 is involved the formation of functional synaptic terminals at the fly neuromuscular junction.

-Deletion of DSyd1 leads to a smaller NMJ, and a reduced number of active zones per NMJ (Figure 4 E-G).
-DSyd1 deletion gives rise to improper localization of active zone proteins BRP (Figure 5) and DLiprin-a (Figure 10)
-Electron microscopy reveals an abnormal organization of the T-bar, a critical morphological component of active zones at the NMJ (Figure 6).
-In addition to presynaptic defects, DSyd1 deletion leads to defects of the postsynapse, including a reduction of PSDs per NMJ (Figure 4 H and the size of GluR clusters (Figure 7)
-DSyd1 deletion results in a reduction of action-potential induced synaptic transmission (figure 4).
-In line with a role in the formation of functional active zones, DSyd1 arrives at nascent synaptic terminals before the active zone marker BRP (Figure 9).

In mammalian synapses, the mSyd1a has been suggested to play a role in active zone organization, but current available data are inconclusive, and homology between mSyd1a and DSyd1 is limited (Wentzel et.al. 2013).

comments.rationale:
By acidification (Fig 8 B) and glutamate uptake assays (Fig. 8 C), Stobrawa et al. show that SVs (LP2 fraction) from ClC-3 KO mice acidify at slower rates and that the glutamate uptake by the SVs is significantly reduced. This data suggests that ClC-3 mediates the Cl- conductance in the majority of the SVs.
In addition VGLUT1 expression in the KO SVs is also reduced together with attenuated glutamate uptake activity of the vesicles (fig. 8C).
Thus, the finding of reduced Cl- conductance in KO mice, considering the reports of other groups, can be alternatively explained by the reduction of VGLUT1 expression rather than the loss of ClC-3.
Overall, additional experimental evidence for the Cl- conductance by ClC-3 is required.

comments.rationale:
Wang et al performed biotinylation experiments in order to verify plasma membrane expression of ClC-3. Shortly, the authors use membrane impermeable NHS-biotin derivate in order to biotinylate plasma membrane proteins exposed to the extracellular surface of cultured rat hippocampal neurons (Fig. 5A). Furthermore, ClC-3 expression on the synaptic plasma membrane surface was examined by preparation of synaptic vesicle and membrane fractions from rat hippocampi followed by immunodetection of ClC-3 and plasma membrane and SV marker proteins (Fig. 5B). In addition, in a double immunogold labeling EM experiment on isolated plasma membrane fraction, PSD95 and ClC-3 surface expression was confirmed. In order to validate the postsynaptic expression of ClC-3, as determined biochemically and by EM, Wang et al perfomed immunofluorescene experiments on cultured rat hippocampal neurons and showed colocalization of the chloride channel with PSD95 and NMDAR (Fig. 6 A and B). comments.rationale:
Whole cell patch recordings of P7-P10 calyxes at 22-24 oC were given a 20 ms depolarization from -80 mV to +10 mV. The initial rate of decay of the capacitance change was significantly slower (~33% of control) in the Actin, beta KO suggesting a slower rate of endocytosis following vesicle fusion (Fig 2. A-C). Similar results were observed when the stimulus was changed to a 20 action potential equivalent stimulus (Fig. 2 D-F), performed at 34-37 oC (Fig. 2 G) and in older mice (P13-P14) (Fig. 2 H).

Hippocampal neurons were cultured from the Actb LoxP/LoxP mice transfected with Synaptophysin-pHluorin2X (SypH) with or without a Cre containing plasmid (Fig. 6 A and D). SypH can be used to study vesicle recycling as it is non-fluorescent in relatively low pH environment of vesicles but is fluorescent in the higher pH extracellular environment. Upon stimulation the decay of fluorescence was significantly slower than the control (Fig. 6 E-G). This fluorescence was quenchable by a low pH solution applied externally indicating it was not a deficit in vesicle reacidification, but instead suggesting that the vesicles had not been endocytosed (Fig. 6H). This effect was rescued by transfecting Actb in the KO cultures (Fig 7 A,B) but was not rescued by a version of Actb that could not polymerize (Fig 7 E,F). Taken together this data suggests that Actin, beta is important for endocytosis.

comments.species:
Transgenic Mice
To reduce PKA activity selectively within the hippocampus and other forebrain regions, we have used the CaMKIIα promoter to express R(AB), an inhibitory form of the RIα subunit of PKA. After purification by CsC1 gradient centrifugation, the CaMKII-R(AB) transgene was purified away from vector sequences by digesting with BssHII. The 11.5 kb transgene was isolated by agarose gel electrophoresis and purified after electroelution using Elutip. Transgenic mice were generated by injecting the purified CaMKII-R(AB) transgene into pronuclei of BL6CBAF2/J zygotes ( Hogan et al. 1994). Founders were backcrossed to C57BL/6J mice. In some cases, because of breeding difficulties, mice from the R(AB)-2 transgenic line were crossed to B6CBAF1/J animals. Mice were maintained and bred under standard conditions, consistent with NIH guidelines and approved by the IACUC. For genotyping, tail DNA was prepared ( Laird et al. 1991) and analyzed by Southern blotting (Sambrook et al. 1989) using a transgene-specific probe.
comments.rationale:
The authors use a transgenic mouse line that overexpresses a dominant negative form of PKA RI alpha to study the role of PKA in long-term plasticity (LTP) at the Schaffer collaterals of the hippocampus. It is found that the late phase of LTP (L-LTP) is abolished in this mouse line, strongly suggesting that PKA is required for L-LTP.

It is well established that LTP at Schaffer collaterals is a postsynaptic process, requiring the recruitment of AMPA receptors. The exact mechanism of action for PKAs is not understood, but requires the phosphorylation of AMPA receptors (Man et. al). PKA RIB is also involved in LTD (Brandon et.al. 1995), a process that regulates synaptic transmission through endocytosis of receptors.

comments.rationale:
A knockout for PKA C1 beta is used to study its role in synaptic plasticity at the mossy fiber synapse. It is shown that removal of C1 beta abolishes LTP at this synapse (figure 2 D and E).

It is well established that LTP at the mossy fiber synapse is a presynaptic process (Zalutsky & Nicoll). Additionally, it's expression does not require potentiation of presynaptic calcium influx (Kamiya et.al.). Therefore, this form of presynaptic LTP must act through potentiation of the synaptic vesicle cycle itself. The PKA substrate(s) required for LTP are unknown.

comments.rationale:
A knockout mouse line for PKA R1 beta is used to study its role in synaptic plasticity. It is shown that long term depression (LTD) at the schaffer collaterals is severely reduced in this mouse line. This demonstrates a role for R1 beta in LTD.

LTD is a postsynaptic process, requiring the endocytosis of AMPA receptors (Beattie et. al.). The exact mechanisms by which PKAs act in LTD is not understood, but requires phosphorylation of GluR1 (Man et.al.).

comments.rationale:
A PKA RII alpha knockout is used to study the role of RII alph in synaptic plasticity. In this mouse line, a reduction in LTP is observed in layer II/III of the visual cortex.

The exact mechanism by which PKAs mediate LTP are unknown. In the hippocampus, PKA mediated phosphorylation of GluR1 is essential for AMPA receptor trafficking (Man et.al.), but it is unkown whether this is also required in LTP in the visual cortex.

comments.rationale:
The authors use a PKA RII beta knockout mouse to study its role in synaptic plasticity in the visual cortex. It is shown that long term depression (LTD) is abolished in layer V of the visual cortex.

LTD is a postsynaptic process that requires the endocytosis of AMPA receptors (Beattie et al.,Kirkwood and Bear). In the hippocampus, PKA-mediated phosphorylation of GluR1 is required for AMPA trafficking. It has not formally been shown if this is also true in LTD in the visual cortex.

comments.rationale:
This study provides extensive characterization of PLC beta1 localization in brain, using immuno-electron microscopy (HRP labeling and immunogold pre- and postembedding).

In CA1 pyramidal cells, PLC beta1 was predominantly detected in somatodendritic compartments, including dendritic spines (Figure 3, 4). No signal was observed in presynaptic terminals. Note that most signal is cytoplasmatic, although some membrane staining is observed. The latter might be due to activity dependent recruitment of PLC to the plasma membrane via its PH or C2 domains. In the cerebellum, PLC beta1 appears to be largely absent from the synapse (figure 8).

A subcellular fractionation for PLC beta1 is also provided (Figure 3A). This result is in agreement with the EM data, but lacks controls.

Extensive characterization of the antibody is provided, including knockout controls in western blot (Figure 1A, immunofluorescence (Figure 1B) and immuno-EM (Figure 3,4).

comments.rationale:
Postsynaptic knock-down (KD) of Complexin-1 and -2 (shRNA stereotactic in vivo injection into CA1 region of the hippocampus) blocks LTP (Fig. 1 F), indicating that Complexin plays a role in postsynaptic membrane fusion events underlying the exocytosis of AMPA receptors during LTP.

NMDA-Receptor mediated LTD is unaffected by postsynaptic Complexin KD (Fig. 1 H).

Block of LTP can be rescued by expression of a shRNA-resitant full-length Complexin-1 variant (Fig. 1 G).

Basal synaptic transmission is not affected by postsynaptic Complexin KD in slices (Fig.2) and cultures (Fig 4B), indicating that Complexin only regulates AMPA-Receptor exocytosis.

comments.rationale:
The paper tests the effect of SCAMP5 knock-down on SV recycling and endocytosis. Rat hippocampal neurons were cotransfected with vGpH (a vesicular glutamate transporter-1 fused with pHluorin), and shRNA against SCAMP5.
Figure 3 describes the endocytosis of SVs following 300 APs at 10 Hz, as monitored by following the vGpH signal, and demonstrates that endocytosis is slowed in the knock-down neurons. The effect can be rescued by the re-expression of SCAMP5.
Figure 4 shows that the knock-down of SCAMP5 impairs endocytosis during stimulation. The neurons are stimulated by an AP train (300 APs at 10 Hz) to evaluate exocytosis, and, following recovery, by a train of 1200 APs at 10 Hz in the presence of Bafilomycin A1 (blocking SV reacidification following exocytosis), to evaluate the size of the recycling SV pool. This experiment demonstrates that the ratio of Endocytosis to exocytosis is lower in SCAMP5 KD neurons, suggesting that the fraction of the released SVs that undergoes endocytosis during the stimulation is lower than in the WT controls. The effect was fully rescued by the re-expression of SCAMP5.

comments.species: Adult flies; Canton S background.
comments.rationale:
orb2-GFP is detected both pre- and post-synaptically in the mushroom body calyx by immuno-EM using anti-GFP antibodies.

In addition, the paper provides evidence of impaired long-term memory in Orb2 mutants, suggesting a role in synaptic plasticity (Fig. 3-4).

Both conclusions are supported by Majumdar et al., Cell 2012, and the loss of long.term memory also in Keleman et al., Nat. Neurosci 2007.

Note that the fruit fly has only two CPEB isoforms agains four in mammals. Orb2 could equally be the functional ortholog of CPEB2, CPEB3, or CPEB4 (or all three at the same time).

comments.species: "Starting from a preparation of purified nerve terminals obtained from rat brain.." from abstract
comments.rationale:
Clathrin-coated vesicles (CCVs), which by nature are coated with the annotated protein, clathrin heavy chain (CHC), are purified from pre-synaptic nerve terminals. The authors demonstrate in figure 2 that the CCVs are from the pre-synaptic compartment because they require osmotic shock to be released (because they are trapped in intact synaptosomes) whereas CCVs from other parts of the cell, including the post-synapse, would not require this treatment. In figure 4 the authors demonstrate by coomassie staining and western blot that the CCVs are highly enriched in CHC and multiple synaptic vesicle (SV) proteins, clearly indicating that CCVs are involved in SV recycling. Figure 7 uses immuno-electron microscopy to demonstrate that CCVs isolated from the pre-synaptic compartment and whole brain show very similar levels of staining for the SV protein synaptophysin, indicating that the major localization of CHC in brain is on CCVs that recycle SVs.

22/5/2017 Pim

From the abstract, "We show that although synaptojanin is recruited by endophilin at bud necks before fission, the knockout of all three mouse endophilins results in the accumulation of clathrin-coated vesicles, but not of clathrin-coated pits, at synapses".

19/6/2017 Pim
The overexpressed endophilin 1 was of rat species. Literal: "A rat endophilin 1 FL-mRFP under control of the CAG promote"
comments.rationale:
The authors generate triple knockout (KO) mice for mouse endophilin 1, 2 and 3. One problem with this paper is that while it CLEARLY demonstrates a vital role for endophilins in synaptic vesicle (SV) recycling, it remains somewhat unclear as to which endophilin isoform is required.

In fig 4, the authors generate cortical neuron cultures from endophilin 1/2/3 triple KO mice. They use synaptopHlourin (both the synaptophysin or vGLUT forms) to monitor SV endocytosis. Following a 10Hz for 30 sec stimulus (300 action potentials) the rate of SV recovery by endocytosis is measured. The triple KO mice show a significant decrease in endocytosis. Importantly, fig 4B/D/E show that this phenotype can be rescues by full-length endophilin 1.

In fig 5 the authors use EM in mouse cortical cultures to demonstrate that the endophilin triple KO mice have a massive accumulation of clathrin-coated vesicles (CCVs). This demonstrates that endophilins are required for uncoating CCVs but not for their formation or fission, but does not distinguish between endophilin isoforms.

19/6/2017 Pim
- The role of endophilin 1 is shown by the rescue of the tripple KO phenotype by over-expression of rat endophilin 1.

comments.species: From the abstract, "Unexpectedly, mice lacking dynamin 1 were able to form functional synapses, even though their postnatal viability was limited. However, during spontaneous network activity, branched, tubular plasma membrane invaginations accumulated, capped by clathrin-coated pits, in synapses of dynamin 1-knockout mice. Synaptic vesicle endocytosis was severely impaired during strong exogenous stimulation but resumed efficiently when the stimulus was terminated".
comments.rationale: The authors generate dynamin 1 knockout (KO) mice. In fig 3 they demonstrate by electron microscopy that in cortical cultures from these mice, there is an accumulation of clathrin-coated profiles that remain attached to the plasma membrane, clearly indicating a deficiency in the fission of clathrin-coated pits. In fig 5 they use synaptopHlourin (both synaptobrevin and synaptotagmin versions) to measure synaptic vesicle (SV) endocytosis. If one compares fig 5A (no baflomycin) to fig 5B (with baflomycin) one sees that during an intense stimulation (30 secs of 10 Hz stimulus) there is a big difference between wt and KO in terms of the amount of SV recycling. However, at the end of the stimulus (30 sec) the rates of recovery and thus the rates of endocytosis are exactly the same (compare the slopes of the black lines in A versus B). Thus, dynamin 1 is required for SV endocytosis only during active stimulation and not during recovery.

comments.species: Littermate offspring obtained from matings of the CSP-α-KO-spHtg line was used for experiments.
comments.rationale:
The SV protein CSPalpha is not essential for synaptic transmission, but acts as a chaperone for SNAP-25 to regulate the synaptic vesicle cycle (i.e. SV recycling and SV priming).

CSPalpha KO NMJ nerve terminals were analyzed by electrophysiology (Fig. 1) and they exhibit a reduction in the RRP due to a defect in vesicle priming (Fig. 1H) - probably due to a loss of SNAP-25 (Fig. 2). Measurements of Synapto-pHluorin (SpH) fluorescence in response to high-frequency trains of action potentials reveals an impairment of vesicle recycling/endocytosis in CSPalpha KO terminals (Fig.4-6).

comments.species: From the abstract, "Although lack of dynamin 3 does not produce an overt phenotype in mice, it worsens the dynamin 1 KO phenotype, leading to perinatal lethality and a more severe defect in activity-dependent synaptic vesicle endocytosis".
comments.rationale: The authors use dynamin 1 knock out (KO) mice, dynamin 3 KO mice and dynamin 1/3 double KO mice. Using cultured cortical neurons with vGlut1-pHlourin, they demonstrate in fig 4B that fluorescence recovery after stimulation, which is indicative of synaptic vesicle (SV) endocytosis is decreased in dynamin 1 KO mice, is not effected in dynamin 3 KO mice, but is dramatically reduced in dynamin 1/3 double KO mice. Thus, dynamin 1 and 3, which together account for the overwhelming majority of brain dynamin, cooperate in supporting optimal rates of synaptic vesicle endocytosis

comments.species: To determine whether DNPI transports glutamate into secretory vesicles, we used heterologous expression in rat pheochromocytoma PC12 cells.
comments.rationale:
The paper is the first description of VGLUT2 (formally called DNPI) as a glutamate transporter.

Figure 7c-e shows the stable expression of VGLUT2 in PC12 cells.

Figure 8a presents the [3H]L-glutamate uptake in a fraction of light membranes that include synaptic-like microvesicles prepared by lysing PC12 cells that stably express VGLUT2. The figure shows that these membranes take up more glutamate then the WT control (where no expression of VGLUT2 can be detected). Figure 8c shows specificity of the transporter to glutamate, since the inclusion of non-lablelled glutamate is blocked [3H]L-glutamate uptake. Non-labelled L-aspartate, D-aspartate, glycine, or γ-aminobutyric acid had no effect on [3H]L-glutamate uptake.

comments.species:
From M&M and results sections:
- The gravin GT mice, also referred to as SSeCKS mutants (Camus et al., 2001), were a gift from Dr. Jacqueline Barra (Institut Pasteur, Paris, France) and backcrossed to a C57BL/6J background for 10 generations.
- LTP was examined at Schaffer collateral-CA1 synapses in mouse hippocampal slices.
- The gravin GT mouse line was generated by a gene trap insertion of the LacZ reporter into the genomic sequence encoding gravin between exon 1A2 and 1B (Fig. 1 K) (Camus et al., 2001).
comments.rationale:
Authors assessed the effect of the loss of Gravin alpha in a transgenic mouse carrying a gene trap insertion of the LacZ reporter into the genomic sequence of gravin, between exon 1A2 and 1B. These animals show a reduction of gravin alpha. They also express a truncated form of the protein that lacks the RII binding site.
These animals show significantly impaired synaptic plasticity (LTP) assessed at Schaffer collateral-CA1 synapses in hippocampal slices. In particular, they show a defect in the PKA activity- and beta-adrenergic receptor-dependent long lasting LTP, which was induced using different stimulation protocols. Moreover, synaptic plasticity induced by beta2-adrenergic receptor activation was also impaired in Gravin gene trap mice.

15/6/2017 Pim
- This paper build on prior knowledge on the functional relation of Gravin, PKA and β2-Adrenergic receptor. Literal from Introduction: "One anchoring protein that recruits PKA to the β2-AR upon receptor occupancy is the anchoring protein gravin. Gravin, also known as Src-suppressed C kinase substrate (SSeCKS), AKAP12, and AKAP250, is a multivalent scaffolding protein that binds PKA and PKC, sequesters calmodulin, and targets phosphodiesterase 4D (PDE4D) to the plasma membrane"

- Gravin alpha KO animals show (Fig.2):
1. Normal basal synaptic transmission
2. Normal E-LTP (requires activation of the calcium/calmodulin-dependent kinase IIα (CaMKIIα), but does not require PKA or de novo protein synthesis )
3. Impaired long-lasting LTP. This form of LTP requires protein synthesis, PKA activity, and β-ARs.
Given the known relationship between gravin and PKA the authors speculate that the problems in ll-LTP are caused by mislocalization of PKA. High levels of the PKA activator forskolin are able to induce LTP in gravin KO animals suggesting that "cell-wide elevation of cAMP to supraphysiological levels overcomes the mislocalization of PKA."
- In gravin KO animals β2-Adrenergic receptor-mediated synaptic plasticity is impaired (Fig.3)
- In Gravin KO mice the PKA-dependent phosphorylation state of the β2-Adrenergic receptor (representing activity states of these proteins) is alterered after fear conditiong (Fig.5). This confirms perturbation of β2-Adrenergic receptor/PKA mechanics in a paradigm that is known to induce hippocampal synaptic plasticity in live animals. The reduced phosphorylation of β2-Adrenergic receptor also results in perturbed downstream signaling as shown by reduced ERK 1/2 phosphorylation.

Conclusions:
- Gravin participates in a mechanism of synaptic plasticity (SynGO term: "regulation of synaptic transmission", or GO-term: regulation of "long-term synaptic potentiation")
- Gravin is a platform for β2-Adrenergic receptor and PKA signaling. This is done by localization of PKA to the β2-Adrenergic receptor so that it can become activated.
- The synaptic location of these processes is not adressed in this paper. The effect of PKA on late-phase LTP in Schaffer collateral synapses is known to reside in the postsynaptic compartment (see f.i. PMID:9716131). Therefore, a postsynaptic location for Gravin in this paper can be inferred.

Final implementation:
(IC) "protein localization to postsynaptic membrane (GO:1903539)" localized_or_maintains_localization_of "cAMP-dependent protein kinase complex (GO:0005952)" regulates "adrenergic receptor signaling pathway (GO:0071875)" regulates "chemical synaptic transmission (GO:0007268)"

Note: last term is more accurately described by: regulates "long-term synaptic potentiation (GO:0060291)"

comments.species: From abstract, "We report here that synaptojanin 1-deficient mice exhibit neurological defects and die shortly after birth".
comments.rationale:
The authors generate synaptojanin 1 knock out (KO) mice. Previous studies had established that synaptojanin is a lipid phosphatase dephosphorylating PtdIns(4,5)P2 to PtdIns(4)P. PtdIns(4,5)P2 interacts with numerous components required for coating of clathrin coated vesicles (CCVs). The KO mice display an accumulation of CCVs in the presynaptic nerve terminal (fig 3) and recovery from synaptic depression following a strong stimulation (10Hz for 200 sec), an indication of SV recycling is strongly reduced in the KO mice.

19/6/2017 Pim
- Justifcation for selected term by expert: "When synaptojanin is null the presynaptic nerve terminal accumulates CCVs (fig 3A/C/D). This not seen in the wt animals (fig 3B) and in fact one almost never observes CCVs in nerve terminals under wt conditions. This is because the clathrin coats are rapidly removed. This observation is entirely consistent with the fact that synaptojanin dephosphorylates PtdIns(4,5)P2 and this PtdIns species is required for the clathrin coating of CCVs. The inference is that if the CCVs can not uncoat, then the SVs can not rejoin the SV functional pool."

comments.species: From materials and methods "Primary neuronal cultures were prepared from hippocampi of P1-P3 Wistar rats".
comments.rationale:
The authors use siRNA to knock down AP180 in cultured rat hippocampal neurons. Using synaptobrevin pHlourin they find a defect in internalization of synaptobrevin. However, there is no defect in internalization of vGlut pHlourin. They thus argue that AP180 is not involved in synaptic vesicle endocytosis per se but in the sorting of synaptobrevin to synaptic vesicles.

27/5/3017 Pim
Expert has selected term 'synaptic vesicle endocytosis (GO:0048488)', and state in the description field: "They thus argue that AP180 is not involved in synaptic vesicle endocytosis per se but in the sorting of synaptobrevin to synaptic vesicles.". AP180 is described in literature as an adapter protein involved in the selection of cargo for clathrin mediated endocytosis. These data show that AP180 does this for some (synaptobrevin), not all (VGlut) SV cargo's. Since synaptobrevin is a SV component I can agree to apply the term 'synaptic vesicle endocytosis (GO:0048488)' to it. In the definition of this term the aggregation of cargo adapters is part of the endocytosis process (so the "regulates...." box does not have to be checked).

So, I agree to this annotation.

comments.rationale:
Study in the calyx of Held synapse to determine the effects of NCS-1 infusion into the presynaptic compartment.

Figure 1a demonstrates that the infusion of NCS-1 leads to a transient (circa 5 minute) facilitation of the presynaptic Ca2+ current (measured very precisely in this synapse).

Figure 1b demonstrates a negative shift in the current-voltage (I-V) curve of Ca2+ channels, suggesting a direct effect of the NCS-1 overexpression on Ca2+ channel properties. The inclusion of BAPTA together with NCS-1 abolished the effect on the I-V curve, suggesting that the effect of NCS-1 on the Ca2+ channels is Ca2+-dependent. Specifically, the 10 to 90% rise time of the Ca2+ current is faster is calyces where NCS-1 is infused, indicating a direct effect on channel properties.

Figure 2 demonstrates that the Ca2+ current facilitation caused by the perfusion of NCS-1 occludes the Ca2+ current facilitation that is usually observed during paired-pulse stimulation.

6/6/2017 Pim
A C-terminal peptide of NCS-1 that lacks the Ca-binding domain does not show the effect mentioned above, but blocks the effect of infused full length NCS-1 (Fig.4). This suggests that the Ca-effects are not mediated by a Ca-binding/buffering function of the protein, and are likely the result of direct interaction with the target protein (VGCC?). The SyNGO term 'calcium ion binding involved in regulation of presynaptic cytosolic calcium levels (GO:0099534)' is not relevant therefore for the NCS-1 protein.

comments.rationale:
Alpha-SNAP supports SV priming by determining the availability of free SNARE components, particularly during phases of high synaptic activity.

Alpha-SNAP KO mice are embryonically lethal (probably due to its function in other cellular membrane trafficking processes) and couldn't be used in the study. Therefore a hypomorph mutant (HYH) was used that results in a 50% reduction in alpha-SNAP protein levels. Synaptic transmission in autaptic hippocampal neuron cultures was unaffected in this mutant (Fig.S5A-E). Beta-SNAP KO mice were generated in this study. Synaptic transmission in autaptic hippocampal neuron cultures was unaffected in beta-SNAP KO mice (Fig.S6).

Therefore, in the study a Beta-SNAP KO / HYH-double mutant was used since the single mutants did not exhibit any phenotypes, indicating that alpha- and betaSNAP have largely redundant functions. Double mutant mice exhibited a 70% reduction in combined alpha/beta-SNAP protein levels in brain homogenates (Fig.4A), an increase in assembled SNARE complexes (Fig.4B) due to a defect in SNARE-complex disassembly, and a small (~25%) reduction in the basal RRP size measured by hypertonic sucrose and high-frequency stimulation, with no changes in the EPSC size (Fig. 4C-F;Fig. 5A-C). 40 Hz and 100 Hz stimulation and calcimycin treatment revealed a strong perturbation in RRP refilling in double mutant neurons during/after high activity and elevated calcium (Fig. 5D-F, 6E-H).

Overexpression of alpha-SNAP in double mutant neurons rescued the phenotype (Fig.7).
Exogenous glutamate application was not changed in the double mutant before or after 100 Hz stimulation, indicating a selective presynaptic effect (Fig.8).
SNARE-binding assays demonstrate that alpha- and beta-SNAP do not differ in their ability to be incorporated in the 20S complex composed of the SNARE-complex, SNAPs and NSF (Fig.S2E), indicating that they do not have different interaction partners in the synapse and probably have largely redundant functions.

comments.rationale:
The paper studies the effect of NCS-1 overexpression in continental rat hippocampal neuron culture. Double patch clamp experiments in paired neurons allow the comparison between presynaptic-transfected and presynaptic-non-transfected neurons. The paper essentially shows that presynaptic overexpression of NCS-1 leads to a switch to activity-dependent facilitation, from the otherwise observed depression in such cultures.

Figure 1 demonstrates that in paired recordings from reciprocally connected neurons depression is seen in non-transfected presynaptic neurons whereas facilitation is seen at NCS-1 presynapticly transfected synapses.
Figure 2 shows that even though the initial EPSC amplitudes are similar between controls and NCS-1-expressing neurons (Figure 2d), facilitation in seen in NCS-1-transfected synapses and depression in controls. This suggests that the effect of overexpression is on activity-dependent, rather than on basal transmitter release.
Figure 4 shows that in NCS-1-transfected synapses continues facilitation is seen during high frequency stimulus trains.

20/01/2021 Dnyanada: P62168 (NCS1_RAT) was chosen on the basis of the biological system in which the experiment was conducted as the species of the overexpressed NCS-1 construct could not be retrieved.

comments.species: From results, "To identify proteins that affect synaptic transmission and plasticity, we performed genetic screens using eyFLP technology ( Newsome et al., 2000; Stowers and Schwarz, 1999 ; Verstreken et al., 2003). These screens allow us to identify flies that carry random chemically induced (EMS) mutations that affect synaptic transmission in photoreceptors, circumventing the organismal lethality associated with these mutations. Flies with mutant eyes were screened by recording electroretinograms (ERGs)...".
comments.rationale: The authors use a screen to identify proteins in Drosophila melanogaster that carry random chemically induced (EMS) mutations that affect synaptic transmission in photoreceptors. This led to the identification of tweek. To demonstrate that tweek is involved in endocytosis, the authors used neuromuscular junctions from third instar larvae. In figure 3C/D they demonstrate that tweek mutants have decreased uptake of the dye FM1-43 into the presynaptic terminal in response to a 10Hz stimulation. Uptake of FM1-43 is well established as a measure of synaptic vesicle endocytosis. In figure 3E/F they use siRNA to knock down tweek, which also leads to decreased FM1-43 uptake.

comments.rationale:
In fig 4b the authors use cortical cultures from control and knockout mice. Using transfected syaptopHlourin they demonstrated that endocytosis, as determined by quenching of pHlourin fluorescence is decreased in KO mice compared to control following a 10 Hz for 30 sec stimulus. In fig 4d they use the same experimental set up to demonstrate that endocytosis is decreased in the KO mice during stimulation.

In fig 3C,D the authors demonstrate that synapses in the KO mice depress faster in response to a 20 Hz train of 1000 action potentials. fig 3E reveals that the readily-releasable pool of synaptic vesicles is smaller in the KO mice.

In fig 5C, the increase in CCVs observed following stimulation of cortical neurons with KCl (driving synaptic vesicle release) is less in KO neurons than in control neurons.

Fig 6 uses immunogold electron microscopy to demonstrate that PIP kinase Igamma is localized to the presynaptic plasma membrane as well as the cytososl and coated endocytic intermediates. In figure 6C, the authors report a strikingly selective localization of PIPKIγ immunoreactivity on membrane regions directly adjacent to clathrin-coated buds while synaptic vesicles were consistently unlabelled.

comments.species: From the abstract, "Syndapin I knockout (KO) mice...".
comments.rationale:
The authors generate a syndapin 1 KO mouse. In figure 3 they use FM1-43 uptake assays to measure endocytosis in cultured hippocampal neurons. At low frequency stimulation there was a very small decrease in FM1-43 dye uptake but at higher frequency stimulation there was larger relative decrease in SV endocytosis when comparing KO to wt. In figure 4 they use EM in the mouse retina. This synapse fires extensively in the dark. Shifting to light causes a strong compensatory endocytosis. The synapses from KO mice showed numerous irregularities when shifting to light including accumulation of clathrin-coated pits at the plasma membrane and alterations in SV size.

In figure 7, the authors use whole-cell recordings from CA1 pyramidal neurons of syndapin I KO mice and observe reduced frequencies of miniature excitatory and inhibitory potentials consistent with a defect in synaptic vesicle recycling in syndapin I KO neurons.

19/6/2017 Pim
- Literal: "Detailed molecular analyses demonstrate that syndapin I plays an important role in the recruitment of all dynamin isoforms, central players in vesicle fission reactions, to the membrane." Since syndapin seems involved in the recruitment of dynamin I do no classify this protein as a "regulator of..." SVE.

SV31 actively transports zinc (zn2+) in a proton-dependent manner.

SV31 is able to bind zinc: Recombinant SV31 expression in NGF-differentiated PC12 cells and measurement of zinc binding activity using a cell-permeable zinc indicator FluoZin-3. Comparison of wild-type SV31 and mutated SV31 (putative zinc-binding sites were mutated) revealed significantly reduced zinc-binding capacities for the mutant (Fig.6c).

SV31 is able to transport zinc in a proton-dependent manner (Fig.7): SV31 proteoliposomes acidified to pH 6.0 containing the indicator FluoZin-1 exhibit an accumulation of luminal fluorescence after addition of 100 uM Zn2+. SV31 proteoliposomes at pH 8.0, and proteoliposomes containing mutated SV31 acidified to pH 6.0 do not exhibit an accumulation of fluorescence after zinc application.

Complexin-3 is expressed in different brain regions in rat (Fig.2B, 3) and mice (3D).

comments.rationale:
Conclusion: "Our study supports the growing consensus that Cplxs (Cplx3 in RBs and Cplx1 and Cplx2 at conventional synapses) act to stabilize fully primed vesicles in a release-ready state and to suppress unregulated Ca2+-dependent spontaneous and asynchronous release of immature vesicles at early stages of the priming process."

Electrophysiological recordings in mouse retina tissue analyzing wildtype- and Complexin-3 KO mice. Mouse retinal bipolar cells only express Complexin-3 and are therefore a good synapse to study the function of this protein (it is known that Complexins are partially redundant and can compensate for the loss of one isoform).

The study demonstrates a loss of phasic release (reduced EPSC amplitude; Fig.1), increase in spontaneous release (mEPSC frequency Fig.2+6) and asynchronous release (Fig. 7). Impaired phasic release was manifested both in a reduced functional RRP and in an increased EPSC latency. The diminished functional RRP likely resulted from the absence of a facilitatory effect of Cplx3 on Ca2+-dependentexocytosis (Fig. 4) rather than from physical vesicle depletion as assessed by electron microscopy (Fig. S1).

comments.rationale:
NTT4 transports neutral amino acids (submillimolar apparent affinity: proline, leucine and low millimolar apparent affinity: glutamine) in a Na+ dependent, Cl- independent manner.

NTT4/SLC6A17 is a transmembrane protein localized to SVs that is highly homologous to the plasma membrane protein SLC6A15. To study the function of NTT4, a chimeric protein was expressed in HEK293T cells, which had the carboxyl terminus replaced with the corresponding region of SLC6A15 for a greater degree of plasma membrane localization (Fig.2). In this experimental system, the uptake of radiolabeled proline into HEK293T cells could be measured (Fig.3). This transport is dependent of extracellular sodium concentration, pH and membrane potential (Fig.4). The uptake of radiolabeled proline into HEK293T cells is inhibited by neutral amino acids (mainly leucine, methionine, proline, Fig.5).

In PC12 cells, expressed wildtype NTT4 is mainly localized to vesicles and colocalizes with Synaptobrevin-2. Ca2+-dependent exocytosis was induced by ionomycin in the presence of 2.2mM calcium and under this conditions, NTT4-dependent proline transport into PC12 cells was enhanced. These findings indicate that NTT4 is coupled in part to the fusion of vesicles with the plasma membrane. NTT4 may be uniquely relevant during periods of intense neuronal activity.

boutons (i.e., symmetric/inhibitory synapse) in the DG was not reduced in Lrrtm3-KO mice (Figures 5D-5F). The thickness and length of excitatory PSD- or GABA-positive boutons were unchanged by ablation of LRRTM3 protein (Figures 5D-5F). "To determine whether excitatory synaptic function is changed as a result of genetic perturbation of LRRTM3, we performed whole-cell recordings from DG granule cells in hippocampal slices from WT and Lrrtm3-KO mice (Figure 6). This paper describes how "knockdown of cortactin by short-interfering RNA (siRNA) results in a decrease of dendritic spines in hippocampal neurons, whereas overexpression of cortactin causes elongation of spines. comments.rationale:
The proline transporter (PROT) is an integral membrane protein expressed in a subset of excitatory (glutamatergic, asymmetric) synapses in different brain regions.

Pre- and postembedding immuno-EM reveals a localization to synaptic vesicles in a subset of glutamatergic terminals (Fig. 4-6). Subcellular fractionation demonstrates that PROT is highly enriched in the purified synaptic vesicle (SV) fraction, similarly to the SV proteins Synaptobrevin-2 and Synaptophysin (Fig.7). Treatment of purified SVs with a mixture of endo- and exoproteases allows the digestion of cytoplasmic domains, indicating that the N- and C-termini of PROT are cytoplasmic (Fig.8). This topology of the PROT protein is 'inverted' with respect to the plasma membrane orientation (See discussion and Fig. 9), indicating shuttling of PROT between SVs and the plasma membrane.

Antibodies: Polyclonal rabbit antibody A2 was produced and affinity-purified by Research Genetics (Huntsville, AL) against residues 2-18 from the predicted N terminus of rat PROT (KKLQEAHLRKPVTPDLL). The affinity-purified polyclonal anti- body directed against the C terminus of rat PROT, antibody C597, has been described previously (Velaz-Faircloth et al., 1995). Both antibodies were tested for its specificity by biochemistry using stably PROT expressing HEK cells and transiently expressing HeLa cells (Fig.1). C597 antibody, preabsorbed with the C-terminal antigenic peptide, did not produce any immunoreactivity by immunohistochemistry (Fig.2D).

Figure 5: immunogold-labelling electron microscopy leads to the finding that the hair cells, as well as the calycal membrane facing the synaptic cleft, both harbor EAAT4 and EAAT5, supporting the notion that the transporters are located at both the pre- and postsynaptic membranes.
Table 1 presents the quantification of the immuogold labeling.
Figure 6 is a summarizing scheme.

comments.species: The isolation of an EAAT subtype from salamander retina whose sequence differed substantially from previously reported mammalian sequences lead us to isolate the human homolog EAAT5.
comments.rationale:
In the paper the isolation of the EAAT5, an excitatory amino acid transporter is described.

In figure 3 the uptake of 3H-L-glutamate and 3H-L-Aspertate are demonstrated in oocytes injected with the EAAT5 mRNA and voltage-clamped at -60 mV. In comparison to controls (uninjected oocytes), the uptake was typically 2- to 10-fold larger. The uptake is sodium- and voltage-dependent.
These data indicate that the transporter functions as a glutamate transporter.
Table 1 summarizes specificity and kinetic values of the transporter.

comments.rationale:
CB1 localized in mitochondria (mtCB1) regulates mitochondrial respiration: using purified mitochondria from wild-type (WT) or CB1-/- brains it is shown that treatment with CB1 receptor agonists WIN (Figure 3) or THC (Figure 4a-c) reduces respiration, cAMP levels and PKA activity in neuronal mitochondria.

Depolarization of CA1 postsynaptic pyramidal neurons mobilizes endocannabinoids, which retrogradely activate presynaptic CB1 receptors, transiently decreasing GABAergic inhibitory neurotransmission in a process known as depolarization-induced suppression of inhibition (DSI), an endocannabinoid-dependent form of short-term plasticity of inhibitory neurotransmission in the hippocampus. DSI is fully blocked by cell-permeant CB1 antagonists (AM251) but only partially blocked by cell-impermeant CB1 antagonists (hemopressin) (Figure 6A), indicating a contribution of mtCB1 activation in DSI. In addition, suppression similar to the one obtained by DSI is found only with cell-permeant agonists of CB1 (HU210) but not with cell-impermeant versions (biotinylated-HU210). Also, HU210 occludes DSI completely, whereas biotinylated-HU210 only occludes it partially, suggesting again a contribution of mtCB1 activation for DSI (Figure 6C). mtCB1 activation also results in reduced mitochondrial respiration and, additionally, direct inhibition of complex I activity using rotenone also mimics DSI, suggesting that endocannabinoid-induced DSI depends on mitochondrial respiration, which would be controlled by mtCB1 (Figure 7).

GENERATION OF VGLUT1VENUS KI MICE.
The targeting vector was constructed on the basis of a 14 kb genomic clone of the VGLUT1 locus in pBluescript, which had been isolated from a λFIXII genomic library of the SV129 mouse strain (Stratagene). In the targeting vector, the STOP codon in the last coding exon (exon 12) of the VGLUT1 gene was replaced in-frame by a venus-loxP-neor-loxP cassette using recombineering techniques with engineered primers. The Venus cDNA was kindly provided by Dr. A. Miyawaki (RIKEN, Wako, Japan), and the recombineering toolbox was provided by Dr. N. Copeland (NCI, Frederick, MD). The venus-loxP-neor-loxP cassette was inserted between a 6.7 kb genomic sequence in 5' position and a 7.9 kb genomic sequence in 3' position (Fig. 1C). Mice carrying the mutated VGLUT1VenusNeo gene (VGLUT1vn/+) were generated by homologous recombination in embryonic stem cells (SV129/ola) as described previously (Thomas and Capecchi, 1987; Augustin et al., 1999) and identified by Southern blotting or PCR (Fig. 1D,E). To eliminate deleterious effects of the neomycin resistance gene, we crossed heterozygous VGLUT1vn/+ mice with EIIa-cre mice that express Cre recombinase in early embryonic stages (Lakso et al., 1996). Successfully recombined VGLUT1Venus alleles (v/+) in offspring from these interbreedings were genotyped by PCR (Fig. 1D). Except for initial comparative analyses of VGLUT1VenusNeo and VGLUT1Venus mice (Fig. 1), Cre recombined VGLUT1Venus mice were used for all experiments. All experiments were performed with littermates derived from crossing heterozygous VGLUT1v/+ or homozygous VGLUT1v/v mice (F2 SV129/ola × C57BL/6 genetic background). All live imaging experiments were performed on VGLUT1v/v mice. The probe used for embryonic stem (ES) cell screening by Southern blot was amplified from the VGLUT1 locus. It is located on the mouse chromosome 7 contig NT_039424.7 at position 6081938-6082223. The following oligonucleotides were used for genotyping PCRs: 9420, CTGGCTGGCAGTGACGAAAG; 9421, CGCTCAGGCTAGAGGTGTATGGA; 9423, CTTCAAGATCCGCCACAACATCG; 4174, CGCATCGCCTTCTATCGCCTTCTT. Oligonucleotides 9420 and 9421 were used to amplify the WT VGLUT1 allele, oligonucleotides 9421 and 9423 were used to amplify the VGLUT1v allele, and oligonucleotides 9421 and 4174 were used to amplify the VGLUT1vn allele.

comments.rationale:
Figure 1C,D: Depolarization of CA1 postsynaptic pyramidal neurons mobilizes endocannabinoids, which retrogradely activate presynaptic CB1 receptors, transiently decreasing GABAergic inhibitory neurotransmission (depolarization-induced suppression of inhibition or DSI) or glutamatergic excitatory neurotransmission (depolarization-induced suppression of excitation or DSE). DSI is lost in CB1 knockout mice (Figure 1C,D). Additionally, DSE is lost in CB1 knockout mice (Figure 8A of Ohno-Shosaku, T. et al (2002) J Neurosci, 22(10), 3864-3872).

Figure 3: In addition, evidence is shown that presynaptic N-Type Ca2+ channels are required for endocannabinoid signaling. DSI is occluded by a specific antagonist of N-type channels, ω-conotoxin GVIA, indicating a presynaptic requirement for N-type calcium channels in the regulation of GABAergic transmission by cannabinoids. Conversely, blocking P/Q-type channels results in increased DSI (removes a component of GABA release that is insensitive to DSI and therefore modulation of N-type calcium channels by cannabinoids is now very relevant).

The brains of adult male Sprague-Dawley rats (2 months old) were fixed and cut into coronal sections with a vibrating microtome.
Mutant mice with targeted inactivation of Cav1.2 expression in the hippocampus (Cav1.2HCKO) were used in antibody verification.
comments.rationale:
Developed an antibody against the pore forming subunit of Cav1.2 that was used in light and electron microscopy of fixed and stained rat brain sections.

Fig. 1 shows characterization and validation of antibody specificity.

Immunoreactivity against the Cav1.2 pore-forming subunit (Cav1.2-IR) was observed in both myelinated and unmyelinated axons. Within labeled axons, Cav1.2-IR was either clustered or filled the intracellular space (Fig. 5A).

Axon terminals were also labeled, especially in CA1 stratum radiatum (Fig. 5B) and dentate gyrus (DG) stratum moleculare and least in CA3 stratum lucidum (Table 1). A majority of the labeled axon terminals formed asymmetric synapses.

Cav1.2-IR was also observed in a large fraction of mossy fiber terminals in CA3 stratum lucidum and DG central hilus (Table 1), which generally formed asymmetric contacts with unlabeled dendrites (Fig. 5C,D). In these terminals, Cav1.2-IR formed clusters along the plasma membrane at synaptic and nonsynaptic sites but was also detected near nonsynaptic junctions with unlabeled dendrites resembling puncta adherentia.

comments.species: "Wild-type mice of either sex (C57BL/6 or CBA) postnatal 15-24 d were used for the majority of the experiments."
comments.rationale: Figure 2A: Paired recordings between synaptically connected cartwheel cells in the presence of GABA receptor antagonists SR95531 allow detecting glycinergic neurotransmission specifically, measuring IPSC. Glycinergic neurotransmission is acutely reduced when presynaptic surface glycine reuptake by GLYT2 is inhibited pharmacologically (ORG25543). IPSC amplitudes ran down soon after drug application (Fig. 2A), declining to 59 ± 11% of baseline within 10-11 min and 3 ± 1% of baseline within 30 min of drug application. Figure 2E: adding exogenous glycine to the whole-cell internal solution in the presynaptic cell occluded the rundown caused by GlyT2 block, showing that the ORG25543 effect was specifically due to loss of glycine availability in the presynaptic terminal. These results show that GLYT2 constitutively supplies glycine for refilling recycling vesicles.

Krox20 Cre/+;Actg LoxP/LoxP mice were created, which knocked out Actin, Gamma in the Calyx of Held. 200 uM parasaggital brain stem slices were cut for capacitance recordings. Actg LoxP/LoxP were used as controls.

Mouse hippocampal cultures were prepared using Actg LoxP/LoxP mice. Mice were transfected with a Cre-mCherry plasmid to create knockout.

8/6/2017
The species of the over-expression construct (Fig.7) is not relevant for species selection since serving as control for specificity of loss of native mouse protein.
comments.rationale:
Whole cell patch recordings of P7-P10 calyxes at 22-24 oC were given a 20 ms depolarization from -80 mV to +10 mV. The initial rate of decay of the capacitance change was significantly slower (~33% of control) in the Actin, Gamma KO suggesting a slower rate of endocytosis following vesicle fusion (Fig 2. A-C). Similar results were observed when the stimulus was changed to a 20 action potential equivalent stimulus (Fig. 2 D-F), performed at 34-37 oC (Fig. 2 G) and in older mice (P13-P14) (Fig. 2 H).

Hippocampal neurons were cultured from the Actg LoxP/LoxP mice transfected with Synaptophysin-pHluorin2X (SypH) with or without a Cre containing plasmid (Fig. 6 A and D). SypH can be used to study vesicle recycling as it is non-fluorescent in relatively low pH environment of vesicles but is fluorescent in the higher pH extracellular environment. Upon stimulation the decay of fluorescence was significantly slower than the control (Fig. 6 E-G). This fluorescence was quenchable by a low pH solution applied externally indicating it was not a deficit in vesicle reacidification, but instead suggesting that the vesicles had not been endocytosed (Fig. 6H). This effect was rescued by transfecting Actg in the KO cultures (Fig 7 A,B). Taken together this data suggests that Actin, Gamma is important for endocytosis.

The authors use a fluorescently labeled overexpression of human b-actin to study the dynamics (G-actin/F-actin transitions) of the actin cytoskeleton in dendritic spines. As inferred by the curator and based on the author's intent it is derived that the b-actin gene provides the structural basis of the F-actin skeleton at the postsynapse.

The "structural component" term is derived from Fig.4 where local application of the actin polymerization inhibitor Latrunculi A resulted in reduction of actin distribution in the synapse and the retraction of the spine. For this reason this term is not annotated against a IC evidence code.

comments.species: Here we report the molecular cloning, expression, deduced amino acid sequence, and apparent molecular size of the canine cardiac sarcolemmal Na+-Ca2+ exchange protein.
comments.rationale:
The paper reports the cloning of the Na+/Ca2+ exchanger (NCX1) from canine and characterizes its transporter activity.

Figure 1 reports an experiment where the NCX1 mRNA was injected in Xenopus oocytes (control- water injected). Na+ gradient-dependent labelled (45)Ca2+ uptake was measured under the following experimental conditions:
-internal Na+ was elevated by incubation with nystatin.
- the external solution contained 10 uM of labelled CaCl2 in a K+ medium, in the absence of external Na+.

Under these conditions, the labeled Ca2+ uptake was at least one order of magnitude greater than control or than previously observed in oocytes injected with poly(A)+ RNA from cardiac tissue (PMID: 2462361).

When the external K+ ions were exchanged for Na+, or when the nystatin treatment was omitted, only background uptake levels were observed, indicating the need for a Na+ gradient for the Ca2+ uptake.

Taken together, the experiment demonstrates that the identified cDNA codes for a Na+/Ca2+ exchanger.

To test whether PTPs mediates TrkC induced presynaptic differentiation, we investigated synapsin clustering around
TrkC-Fc-coated beads that contacted axons expressing either HA-PTPs or HA-PTPs lacking the intracellular domain
(HA-PTPsDICD). TrkC-Fc-coated beads induced HA-PTPs clustering accompanied by synapsin clustering on axons (Figures 4D and 4E). TrkC-induced synapsin clustering associated with HAPTPs was equivalent to TrkC-induced synapsin clustering on
neighboring nontransfected axons (Figure 4E), suggesting that
HA-PTPs is comparable in activity to the endogenous presynaptic
receptor of TrkC. In contrast, TrkC-Fc-coated beads that
induced HA-PTPsDICD clustering on axons did not induce simultaneous clustering of synapsin (Figures 4D and 4E). Presumably, HA-PTPsDICD effectively competed with endogenous PTPs for TrkC binding and blocked transmembrane signaling from TrkC to axonal intracellular targets for presynaptic differentiation. Taken together, these data suggest that PTPs is an axonal receptor for TrkC that triggers presynaptic differentiation.
Next, we tested whether PTPs ectodomain triggers excitatory
postsynaptic differentiation associated with dendritic accumulation of TrkC. PTPs-Fc-coated beads that contacted dendrites induced clustering of endogenous dendritic TrkC with NMDA receptor subunit NR1 (Figure 4F). NR1 clusters induced by
PTPs-Fc-coated beads were not apposed to synapsin (Figure
4G), indicating that these NR1 clusters were not associated with interneuronal synapses. PTPs-Fc-coated beads also induced clustering of PSD-95 but not of gephyrin (Figures 4H and 4I). We also confirmed in the coculture assay that COS cells expressing PTPs-CFP induced clustering of NR1 (data not shown) and of PSD-95 but not of gephyrin (Figure S4G) on contacting
dendrites. These data indicate that PTPs acts as a presynaptic factor to induce excitatory postsynaptic differentiation
and suggest that its postsynaptic receptor is TrkC."

comments.rationale:
The paper reports the cloning and functional characterization of NCX2 as a Ca2+/Na+ exchanger. The authors use 'inside out' patches from Xenopus oocytes expressing NCX2.
The patch pipette, facing the extracellular side, contains 8 mM Ca2+ and no Na+.
The external solution, facing the cytoplasmic side of the membrane patch, contains 100 mM cesium. Figure 5a shows that a current can be elicited when the cesium is replaced by Na+, in the presence of 1, or 3 microMol Ca2+ in the external solution. When no Ca2+ is present at the external solution, no current is elicited, indicating a requirement of Ca2+ at the cytoplasmic domain of the exchanger.
Figure 5b shows that when the Ca2+ is removed from the external solution, the current decays.
Figure 5d shows the IV curve for the exchanger.

The data presented indicates a function for NCX2 as a Na+/Ca2+ exchanger that is dependent on the ion gradients.

* 'Therefore, we subcloned a poly(A)1-containing fragment of DNA into the BglII-NotI site of pIII (Fig. 1). This replaced most of the original NCX3 39-UTR with the 39-UTR derived from the SGLT1 (Na1-glucose cotransporter) clone (Hediger et al., 1987)'
