Figure 7, A and B: Fluorescence microscopy targeted towards intracellular and total GluA2 was used to calculate the GluA2 internalisation index. TSPAN7 Knockdown demonstrated an increase in the GluA2 internalisation index indicating its role as a regulator in GluA2 trafficking in the post-synapse. To ascertain that the effect was a true representation of endocytosis of GluA2 receptor, a similar experiment in the presence of dynamin inhibitor Dynasore was carried out. Dynasore abolished the differences in the internalization index between TSPAN7-knockdown and scrambled siRNA14 neurons.
Figure 8 A: Rescue WT rescues the effect of TSPAN7 knockdown by reducing the internalization index close to control levels. Overexpression of TSPAN7 reduces the GluA2 internalization index compared to control.

comments.species:
Syt12 S97A KI and Syt12 KO mice were generated using homologous recombination in embryonic stem cells targeting exon 4 of the Syt12 gene.
Syt12 S97A KI = A ~15 kb genomic clone containing exon 4 up to the 3' untranslated region (UTR) was isolated using a 32P-labeled probe for exon 4 of Syt12, which was amplified with primers YJ0601 (GCTGTCACCTAGCGATGGTGCC) and YJ0602 (CACGATCTGT TCGTCTGGCAGC). The targeting vector contained a Ser-97-Ala mutation in exon 4, and exon 4 - 6 were flanked with loxP sites for Cre recombination; neomycin resistance gene flanked by frt sites was introduced at a nonconserved region between exon 5 and 6, and a diphtheria toxin (DT) expressing cassette was inserted at the end of 3' UTR.

Syt12 KO = Flp recombinase transgenic mice were used to remove the neomycin resistance cassette for Syt12 S97A KI, followed by breeding to protamine-Cre transgenic mice to generate constitutive Syt12 KO.

Homologous recombination was achieved by electroporation of the linearized targeting construct in R1 embryonic stem cells and positive clones were isolated by drug selection and screened by Southern blotting and PCR genotyping. Clones with confirmed homologous recombination were then injected into C57BL/6 blastocysts
comments.rationale:
Fig 7A and D: Representative traces of mossy fibre field-EPSPs (fEPSPs) before (trace 1) and after (trace 2) induction of mossy fibre LTP in acute slices from littermate WT, Syt12 S97A KI and Syt12 KO mice. mfLTP was induced by two 25 Hz/5 s stimulus trains separated by 20 s and applied in the presence of the NMDA-receptor antagonist d-APV (50 μm) that was washed out immediately after induction. After each individual mfLTP experiment, the slice was exposed to 1 μm DCG-IV, a group II mGluR agonist, to determine the relative contribution of mossy fibre synaptic inputs to the fEPSP.
Figure 7B and E: Mossy fibre fEPSP amplitudes plotted as a function of time before and after mfLTP induction (arrow). Syt12 S97A KI and Syt12 KO mice show a reduction in EPSP amplitude relative to WT.
Figure C and F: Distributions for the magnitude of LTP observed in each genotype were plotted. Significant reduction (~50%) in the magnitude of mfLTP was seen for both Syt12 S97A KI and Syt12 KO mice.

In order to limit the contribution of the population of action potentials in the results, the paper conducted whole-cell recording experiments to check for the effect of Syt12 mutation. Representative traces are displayed in Figure 8A.
Figure 8 B and C: Mossy fibre NMDA-receptor EPSC amplitudes plotted as a function of time before and after mfLTP induction display a reduction in the Syt12 S97A KI condition. Distribution of mfLTP magnitude demonstrated a ~50% reduction in the magnitude of mfLTP for Syt12 S97A KI condition.
Figure 8D: Consistent with its presynaptic expression, mfLTP in WT mice was associated with a decrease in PPR, whereas mfLTP was not accompanied by a significant change in PPR in Syt12 S97A KI mice.

Since the effects of Syt12 KO and Syt12 S97A KI were similar on the magnitude of mossy fibre LTP, the paper proposes that phosphorylation of Syt12 may be required for the expression of LTP in mossy fibres.

comments.species: Cpne6 KO mice were generated by homologous recombination (illustrated in Supplementary Fig. 1a), using a cassette in which the entire protein-coding region of Cpne6 (exon 2-16) was replaced by nls-LacZ. Gene targeting was carried out in embryonic stem cells (75% C57BL/6, 25% 129 Sv). The targeting vector contained 5 kb of 5'-arm (Cpne6 promoter, exon 1, intron 1 and a small part of exon 2) followed by nls-LacZ-SV40 polyA signal-LoxP-PGKneo-LoxP and 3 kb of 3'-arm (Cpne6 exon 16, intron 16, exon 17 and 3'-downstream sequence) followed by MC1-HSV-TK (for negative selection). Chimeric mice were obtained by microinjection of correctly targeted embryonic stem cell clones into C57BL/6 blastocysts. The LoxP-flanked neo-cassette was removed by intercrossing mice with Hprt-are (Cre-deleter) mice. Genotypes were identified by PCR flanking the 5'-end with following specific primers: Gt5F (5'-TGC AGC ACT GGC TCA TAG AC-3'), Gt5R (5'-GGA AAG TCC TTG GGG TCT TC-3') and Gt5wtR (5'-GCA CCC ATC CCA TCT CTG-3') or at the 3'-end: Gt3R (5'-ATC TGA GGC ATG ACG GGT AG-3'), Gt3wtF (5'-CTA TGA CTC CCA GCC CTA GC-3') and Gt3F (5'-CAC TGC ATT CTA GTT GTG GTT TG-3').
comments.rationale:
Rac1 is part of the Rac1-PAK-LIMK1-Cofilin signalling pathway that is crucial for actin reorganisation in the postsynapse. To test whether CPNE6 regulates this pathway, co-expression experiments were carried out.

Figure 5a and b: CPNE6 coimmunoprecipitates with RAC1 derived from Cos7 and hippocampal neuron lysates.
Figure 5e: Co-expression of CPNE6 resulted in a strong increase in the total amount of active Rac1-GTP
Figure S8c: CPNE6 recruits RAC1-PAK complex to the plasma membrane and activates Rac1 in cos7 cells.
Figure S9a: Cofilin was not significantly increased in spines of Cpne6 KO neurons on cLTP indicating defective Rac1-PAK-LIMK1-Cofilin signalling.
Figure S9b: Phosphorylation of Cofilin was reduced in CPNE6 hippocampal cultures compared to WT.

Figure 6d: Extracellular field potential recordings of hippocampal slices show a reduction in fEPSP slope compared to WT. This effect was neutralised with the addition of jasplakinolide (a toxin that stabilised newly formed actin filaments) further solidifying the role of cpne6 in the stabilisation of subsynaptic actin cytoskeleton.

The 'regulates' box was ticked because CPNE6 was shown to phosphorylate Cofilin (Figure S9b) and regulate the Rac1-PAK-LIMK1-Cofilin signalling pathway required for actin organisation.

CAP is known to play a role in dissociation of the cofilin-G-actin-ADP complex for actin polymerisation (Moriyama and Yahara, 2002). To study if CAP2 interacts with cofilin in neurons:

Taken together, CAP2 mutants demonstrate actin accumulation and impaired actin dynamics (in terms of F-actin and activated n-cofilin distribution)
The SynGO term presynaptic cytoskeletal organisation was used based on the co-localisation studies of CAP2 with synapsin I (shows overlap in the presynaptic terminal, Supplementary S1C, D) and PSD-95 (localises adjacent to PSD-95, Figure 1E)

comments.rationale:
While the evidence is weak, immunofluorescence staining of SCRN1 using rabbit anti-SCRN1 (Sigma, HPA024517, RRID:AB_2184811) shows presynaptic localization of SCRN1 by co-localization with vGlut1 (presynaptic marker). The antibody is validated in supplementary Fig EV1I and EV1J where neuronal staining of SCRN1 is reduced in neurons expressing an shRNA against SCRN1. EV1H displays that the antibody used for SCRN1 is specific and does not cross-react with other isoforms.

In addition, human SCRN1a was fused to GFP and expressed in rat primary hippocampal neurons. Presynaptic co-localization of SCRN1-GFP and Syt1 staining is observed and shown in figure EV1 F. The presynaptic phenotype in SCRN1 knockdown neurons was rescued by expressing wild-type GFP-SCRN1, indicating that SCRN1-GFP construct retains its function despite the GFP tagging.

11/01/2021 Dnyanada:
The co-localisation of SCRN1 with the presynaptic marker Syt1 (Figure 1I) should be considered with scepticism as the experiment does not include a negative control (post-synaptic marker) to indicate an exclusive presynaptic localization.
The paper also shows that GFP-SCRN1 colocalises with the ER luminal marker TagRFP-ER in hippocampal neurons (Figure 2) indicating its localisation in the presynaptic SER. However, the generic term "presynapse" was chosen as it is based on overexpression of the gene and fails to represent its endogenous location.

Synaptic vesicle cycling was stimulated in neuronal cultures by applying 50 uM bicuculline for 10 min at 37°C. Antibody used was mouse anti-synaptotagmin (SySy, 105311, clone 604.2).

18/01/2021 Dnyanada: Using expansion microscopy, SCRN1knock-down demonstrates an altered ER nanoscale organization in terms of discontinuity of the ER tubules in axons, and overall less dense and irregular ER structures in axons, dendrites, and soma. FRAP experiments expressing SCRN1 knock-down also demonstrate discontinuous ER structures (~40% reduction in ER marker TagRFP-ER) indicating impaired ER dynamics. Based on this and the results from the synaptotagmin uptake assay (as described in the annotation), the term "regulation of synaptic vesicle cycle" was used.

comments.rationale:
"Anoctamin-6 / TMEM16F promotes Ca2+-Activated Cl Conductance in spinal motoneurons"
-In Fig 1, different electrophysiological recordings are carried out to measure Ca2+-activated Cl conductance in motoneurons. In established conditions to prevent Na+ and K+ currents, we can observe an outward current (depolarization) and tail inward (repolarization) after applying voltage ramps from -100 mV to +20 mV. They developed these assays in motoneurons electroporated with control siRNA or specific siRNAs against Tmem16 genes, observing a significant decrease in outward and inward currents for the siRNA-Tmem16f condition and not for the others (Figs. D and E), which suggest the specific role of TMEM16F for Cl conductance in motoneurons.

Notes:

-In Fig. 2B, they showed successful siRNAs electroporation observing rhodamine positive motoneurons before to carry out the electrophysiological recordings.

- Moreover, we observed a similar result to Tmem16f RNA inhibition in (Figs. 1F-1I) when they use for the experiments motoneurons with targeted deletion of exon 3 of Tmem16 (strategy in Fig. S2A)

11/01/2021 Dnyanada: Members of Tmem16/Anoctamin family (calcium-activated chloride channels; CACCs) lie in close proximity of calcium channels and regulate the activity of chloride channels (PMID: 22500639). The paper demonstrates that TMEM16F regulates the functional expression of CACCs in motorneurons and as a product governs Ca2+ activated Cl conductance in motorneurons. The paper also shows that TMEM16F might be localised in the postsynapse. Based on the role of TMEM16F in chloride conductance and its localisation in the postsynapse, the term "regulation of postsynaptic membrane potential" was chosen.

comments.rationale:
"Pharmacological inhibition of mGlu2 increases glutamate release probability promoting thalamocortical transmission"
In the experiments shown in this paper, cfos-EGFP or C57BL/6J mice are injected with a control/vehicle solution (eg. DMSO) or Negative Allosteric Modulators (NAMs) solutions for mGlu2 (VU6001966) and for mGlu3 (VU0650786, this protein will be not described in this annotation). After, slices from these mice are prepared to carry out electrophysiological recordings.
In Fig.2, cFos-GFP-positive cells (which were activated by inhibiting mGlu2 with NAM) present a higher hyperpolarization sag, amplitude and frequency of AMPA-receptor-mediated spontaneous excitatory postsynaptic currents (sEPSCs) after mGlu2 NAM administration with respect to control condition.
In Figs.3D-E, we observe again a notable increase of sEPSC amplitude and frequency after mGlu2 NAM administration (in slices from not cfos-EGFP mice this time), suggesting that inhibition of this receptor can stimulate glutamate transmission into the prefrontal cortex (PFC).
In Fig.4, we can see how NAMs administration affects the axis Mediodorsal nucleus of the thalamus-Prefrontal cortex (MDT-PFC) in terms of glutamate transmission and it is studied in slices from mice where it is possible to visualize the optogenetic protein ChR2 (virally expressed previously). An increase of optically-induced EPSC and a decrease of paired-pulse ratio (PPR) is observed after mGlu2 NAM administration, findings that supporting an increase in presynaptic glutamate release probability when mGlu2 is inhibited.
Notes:
In Fig.1, a significant increase of cFos-positive cells is observed after mGlu2 NAM administration, indicating that inhibition of this receptor promotes the activation of the prefrontal cortex. In this case, the technique used is immunohistochemistry, not electrophysiology.
In Fig.5, following with the study of the MDT-PFC axis at thalamocortical synapses, it is shown that mGlu2 NAM partially reduces postsynaptic long-term depression (LTD) in the PFC.

comments.species: Wild-type adult FVB mice were used for the preparation of the mouse cerebellar slices.
comments.rationale:
In the previous CC annotation for mGluR4 (ID 1579) it is described that mGluR4 is highly enriched at active zones (AZs) of membranes from different neuronal layers, but in this new annotation, we provide new data on spatial arrangement and stoichiometry of mGluR4 within these AZs.

In Fig 1B-D, by direct stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy (dSTORM) we can observe a significant number of mGluR4 localizations within parallel fibers active zones (AZs). Previous to this experiment, stainings with a specific mGluR4 antibody (tested in mGluR4 knockout mice in another publication) and bassoon (scaffold protein useful to mark AZs) were carried out.

In Fig 2, using dSTORM and Density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise (DBSCAN), it is determined that mGluR4 is organized in small nanoclusters within AZs with a higher density or concentration inside than outside AZs. Moreover, In Fig S2 B-D, it is shown that mGluR4 follows a quite homogenous distribution within the AZs.

In Fig 3 C-D, we can find that mGluR4s mainly present 2 subunits, it means they appear like a dimer the most of the times. In this case, they used a different model for the experiments, Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells transfected with SNAP-tagged mGluR4s and then labeled with Alexa Fluor 647 to be imaged by total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) microscopy (Fig 3 A-B).

Lastly, this paper establishes that we can approximately find 35 mGluR4 subunits per AZ (data are shown in Figs S4 and S5). In this case, they use the previous named CHO cells and limiting and saturating of mGluR4 primary antibody, and dSTORM imaging to estimate the number of localizations per mGluR4 nanocluster.

Note:
In Fig 6, we can observe an illustrative scheme of mGluR4 nanoscale spatial organization within the actives zones of parallel fibers.

comments.species:
Adult (8-12-week-old) C57BL/6J male mice (Jackson Laboratories, Stock No: 000664) and transgenic cfos-EGFP mice (Jackson Laboratories, Stock No:
014135).
comments.rationale:
"Pharmacological inhibition of mGlu3 stimulates prefrontal cortex (PFC) excitatory transmission"
In the experiments shown in this paper, cfos-EGFP or C57BL/6J mice are injected with a control/vehicle solution (eg. DMSO) or Negative Allosteric Modulators (NAMs) solutions for mGlu3 (VU0650786). After, slices from these mice are prepared to carry out immunohistochemistry experiments and electrophysiological recordings.

In Fig.1, we can observe a notable increase of cFos-positive cells after mGlu3 NAM administration in comparison with control/vehicle condition, it determines that inhibition of this receptor promotes the activation of the prefrontal cortex.

In Fig.2, it is shown higher hyperpolarization sag, amplitude, and frequency of AMPA-receptor-mediated spontaneous excitatory postsynaptic currents (sEPSCs) in cFos-GFP-positive cells after mGlu3 NAM administration with respect to control condition.

In the Fig.5E, we can see how mGlu3 NAM administration affects the axis mediodorsal thalamus (MDT)-PFC at thalamocortical synapses, partially reducing/blocking postsynaptic long-term depression (LTD) in the PFC. In this study, they use slices from mice where it is possible to visualize the optogenetic protein ChR2 (virally expressed).

comments.species:
Mouse C57BL/6J from Jackson Laboratory and Mouse Lrrtm4 RK-KI generated in this paper.
Monkey COS7 cells from ATCC
comments.rationale:
*It is known that neurexins (Nrxs) proteins participate in the synapse assembly process (we can find some related SynGo annotations for Nrx1-alfa (ID 894) / beta (ID900)) and one of their postsynaptic ligands are LRRTMs proteins. In this paper, it is shown that Nrx1-gamma is a novel presynaptic organizer and interacts with LRRTM3/4 through the heparan sulfate (HS) Nrx domain.

-In Fig 5 (D-E), we can observe in hippocampal neurons how LRRTM4 binds to Nrx1-gamma but not to Nrx1-gamma with the HS site at serine 316 mutated to alanine (indicated like "delta-HS" in the paper).
In Fig 5 (G-H) using a COS7-neuron co-culture assay with a silencing for Nrxs (shNrx neurons), it is determined that the overexpression of Nrx1-gamma restores the synaptogenic activity of LRRTM3 and 4, but not LRRTM1 and 2, which is observed through of a higher Synapsin clustering.
Also, in Fig 5F it is shown a co-immunoprecipitation of LRRTM4/3 with Nrx1-gamma (in absence of heparinase treatment) indicating the role of this Nrx1 as an endogenous transsynaptic partner.

In Fig 6, it is suggested a reduction in the number of excitatory synapse in dentate gyrus granule cells (where LRRTM3/4 are highly located) with Nrx1-gamma silenced.

-In Fig 8 (J-K), we can see in an "in vivo" model how the disruption of LRRTM4-Nrxs interaction alters the synaptic function. In this case, they use a knockin mouse mimic Mutation5 (described in Fig2 of this paper, it consists of the mutation of 2 residues of arginine and lysine to alanine for LRRTM4 sequence and results in an alteration of LRRTM4-NRxs binding through HS site).
From synaptosomes of this Lrrtm4 RK-RI mouse, they observe a lower LRRTM4-Nrxs co-immunoprecipitation (for alfa, beta, and gamma) than in WT mice.

Note:
In Fig 5A and FigS5, it is shown that Nrx1-gamma has an HS modification site like alfa/beta transcripts and that this protein is expressed in the neuronal surface.

comments.species: Cerebella of 1-wk-old C57BL/6J mice were dissociated as described previously (Fiszman et al. 2005). comments.rationale:
Figure 4B: Application of NPY5R antagonist L-152,804, prevented NPY induced increase in the frequency of mIPSCs.
Figure 4C-E: Application of another NPY5R antagonist CGP 71683 had a similar effect on the NPY induced increase in the frequency of mIPSCs. Neither L-152,804 nor CGP 71683 applied alone altered mIPSC frequency or amplitude. DMSO at the concentration used to dissolve the antagonists also did not alter the NPY-induced I-LTP.
Figure 5A and C: Coapplication of NPY1R and NPY2R antagonists BIBP3236 (BIBP) and BIIE-0246 (BIIE) did not prevent NPY-induced increase in GABA release characterising the specific role of NPY5R in the process.
Figure 5D-F: Application of NPY5R agonist induced a sustained increase in mIPSC frequency that mimicked the NPY-induced increase in spontaneous GABA release.

Dilp2-GFP was driven directly by the native neuronal synaptobrevin promoter to label DCVs in transgenic flies. This line was further modified by recombination with OK6-GAL4, which was used to drive UAS-Mop RNAi and overexpression constructs in motor neurons.
For controls, UAS lines were crossed to the nsyb-Dilp2-GFP line without a GAL4 driver.
For mop mutant studies, nsyb-Dilp2-GFP was crossed to w*; mopT482 P{neoFRT}80B/TM6B,Tb to generate a stock of w; nsyb-Dilp2-GFP/CyO; mopT482 P{neoFRT}80B/TM6B. This stock was then crossed to the mop allele y w; P{EPgy2}mopEY06090, and non-Tb larvae with the mutant combination of mopT482/P{EPgy2}mopEY06090 were selected for analysis.
Experiments to determine the age of DCVs were done by using ANF tagged fluorescent timer protein monomeric mK-GO.
comments.rationale:
Figure 1 and S1: Increase in synaptic neuropeptide in Myopic-overexpressing and -deficient motoneurons is not accounted for by altered DCV content, transport, or bouton size, but is consistent with an increase in synaptic DCV number.

To check if the increase in neuropeptide storage stems from decreased neuropeptide secretion, the paper investigates if PTPN23 mutation/ overexpression causes an accumulation of older DCVs in boutons.

Figure 2: Neuropeptide-timer construct [atrial natriuretic factor tagged with monomeric Kusabira Green Orange (ANF-mK-GO) driven by 386Y-GAL4] that converts from green to red fluorescence over hours was used. Green/red fluorescence ratios showed that PTPN23 knockdown or overexpression each produced older DCVs compared with control animals.

Figure 3D and E: PTPN23 heterozygous mutant (T482/P) showed a mild change in fluorescence intensity over time for neuropeptide Dilp2-GFP indicating that PTPN23 might inhibit DCV exocytosis.

Figure 3F and G: PTPN23 overexpression completely inhibits DCV exocytosis.

Figure 4A-D: Neuropeptide release was induced by tonic depolarization induced by application of elevated extracellular K+. Even in strong depolarising conditions, PTPN23 RNAi and overexpression reduced the neuropeptide release significantly.

Figure 4E-H: cAMP-evoked synaptic neuropeptide release was also inhibited dramatically by both RNAi and overexpression of PTPN23. This indicates that PTPN23 directly regulates DCV secretion machinery rather than an indirect regulatory effect via voltage-gated Ca2+ channel.

The 'regulate' box was ticked on the basis of the residual neuropeptide release observed in PTPN23 KO (Figure 3, D and E) indicating that it regulates the process.

comments.species: GFP-expressing male larva (i.e., shits1/y; Ok6-GAL4 UAS-Dilp2-GFP/+) were used for confocal imaging of boutons, which was performed at 22°C or after heating to 30°C. Dynamin inhibition at the elevated temperature in these flies was verified by the block of depolarization-evoked FM4-64 (Molecular Probes, Eugene, OR) uptake into SSVs (Ramaswami et al., 1994).
comments.rationale:
To test whether dynamin affects activity-dependent neuropeptide release at the Drosophila NMJ, GFP-tagged prepro-Drosophila insulin-like peptide 2 (Dilp2) was expressed in wild-type (WT) animals and the temperature-sensitive dynamin mutant shits1. Release at the larval neuromuscular junction was evoked by tetanic nerve stimulation (70 Hz, 1 min) at 22°C (i.e., a permissive temperature) or after heating to 30°C to acutely inactivate shits1

Figure 1 A and B: Temperature change did not affect synaptic neuropeptide release in WT animals.
Figure 1 C and D: Temperature-dependent dynamin inhibition halved activity-evoked peptide release.

Temperature-dependent dynamin inhibition does not affect presynaptic Ca2+ responses to activity (Macleod et al., 2004). Therefore, at a native synapse, dynamin directly enhances activity-evoked peptide release.

comments.species: The 3780-bp unc-31 cDNA (derived from PMID: 16272411) under the control of the rab-3 promoter was constructed for genetic rescue. The 1.2 kb rab-3 promoter was amplified by PCR and subcloned to pPD49.26 (1997 Fire Lab Vector Kit) to gain pPD49.26-Prab-3.
comments.rationale:
The paper uses high-resolution membrane capacitance (Cm) measurement combined with Ca2+-uncaging stimuli to monitor the effect of Unc31 KO in DCV exocytosis (as described in PMID:18031683).

Figure 1A: Under Step-like elevations in intracellular calcium, membrane capacitance was significantly reduced in Unc31 mutant (unc-31e928) relative to WT indicating that Unc31 mutants defect exocytosis in ALA neurons of C. elegans. The exocytotic defect was fully rescued by reintroduction of full-length unc-31 cDNA.

comments.species:
Transgenic strains were generated by injecting pkc-1(nj3) and the expression construct with the coinjection markers KP#708 (Pttx-3::rfp), KP#1338 (Pttx-3::gfp) or pPD118.33 (Pmyo-2::gfp) using standard methods (PMID: 1935914)

pkc-1 constructs that rescued pkc-1(nj3) mutants were: KP#1374, KP#1375, KP#1376, KP#1377. KP#1374 contains pkc-1B cDNA and a 3,214-bp unc-17 promoter fragment. KP#1375 contains pkc-1A cDNA and the unc-17 promoter fragment. KP#1376 contains pkc-1B cDNA and a 3,011-bp snb-1 promoter fragment. KP#1377 contains pkc-1B with an ~4-kb pkc-1 promoter fragment.
comments.rationale:
In C. elegans, secreted proteins are endocytosed and degraded by specialized scavenger cells termed coelomocytes. Once taken up by coelomocytes, fluorescent proteins accumulate within endolysosomal organelles, which can be visualized as large internal fluorescent patches. Proneuropeptide genes NLP-21-yellow fluorescent protein (YFP) or INS-22-YFP were expressed in cholinergic motor neurons (using the unc-129 promoter) and were detected in coelomocytes (Figure 7a). In order to ensure that the fluorescent patches are indicative of neuropeptides, soluble YFP or GFP-SNB-1 was expressed in motor neurons (using the same promoter) and it failed to produce detectable coelomocyte fluorescence (Figure 7b).

Figure 7 C and D: Coelomocyte fluorescence decreased by 40% in PKC-1 mutants. This defect was completely rescued by restoring the expression of PKC-1 in cholinergic neurons using the unc-17 promoter. Unc-31 mutants were used as a positive control in the experiment.
These results suggest that PKC-1 acts in motor neurons promote neuropeptide secretion.

In order to verify that PKC1 effects DCV release and not the production or transport of neuropeptides, distribution of NLP-21 and INS-22 fluorescence puncta was quantified in the ventral cord of PKC-1 mutants.
Figure 8 B and C: NLP-21 and INS-22 puncta fluorescence were both significantly increased (~25%) in pkc1 mutants and the effect was rescued by transgenes expressing PKC-1 in cholinergic neurons. NLP-21-YFP and INS-22-YFP puncta fluorescence increased similarly in unc-31 CAPS and unc-13 Munc13 mutants. Unc-31 CAPS and unc-13 Munc13 mutants are known to play a vital role in DCV exocytosis.

Concluding from Figure 7 and Figure 8, PKC1 is responsible for regulating presynaptic dense-core vesicle exocytosis. The term 'regulating' was used on the basis of the kinase activity of PKC1 protein.

comments.species: The rab10 gene was PCR amplified from a cDNA library (ProQuest; Invitrogen). all C. elegans rab genes were cloned and mutated via site-directed mutagenesis to generate dominant-active and dominant-negative variants. The following are the list of dominant-active mutations that were introduced: rab-1 Q70L, rab-2 Q65L, rab-3 Q81L, rab-5 Q78L, rab-6.1 Q70L, rab-6.2 Q69L, rab-7 Q68L, rab-8 Q67L, rab-10 Q68L, and rab-11.1 Q70L. The following are the list of dominant-negative mutations that were introduced: rab-1 25N, rab-2 S20N, rab-3 T36N, rab-5 S33N, rab-6.1 T25N, rab-6.2 T24N, rab-7 T23N, rab-8 T22N, rab-10 T23N, and rab-11.1 S25N. All mutated rab genes were cloned into the pGBKT7 vector as bait.
comments.rationale:
Figure 1A: DCV secretion from cholinergic motoneurons was assayed using a transgenic strain (nuIs183) expressing the proneuropeptide NLP-21 tagged to YFP exclusively in dorsally projecting cholinergic motoneurons. This strain has been successfully used to assay DCV biogenesis and release. At the trans-Golgi, the proneuropeptide NLP-21-YFP fusion is packaged into DCVs, where it is subsequently processed into active neuropeptides and soluble YFP. YFP-labeled DCVs are then transported to axonal release sites. After fusion, the soluble YFP is released into the body cavity. Here, it is constitutively endocytosed by macrophage-like cells, called coelomocytes. The YFP fluorescence in coelomocytes can, therefore, be used as an indirect readout for DCV release.

Figure 1B and S1: To identify Rabs that are regulating DCV release, all viable rab mutants were screened for defects in NLP-21-YFP secretion resulting in low coelomocytes fluorescence. As a positive control, we used unc-31/CAPS mutants, which are known to have defects in DCV release.

Figure 1C: Expression of constitutively active RAB-10 Q68L mutant also led to strongly impaired DCV secretion, whereas DCV release was completely abolished in the rab-10 (ok1494) deletion mutants indicating that Rab10 plays a vital role in regulating DCV exocytosis.

Figure S2: DCV secretion defect of rab-10 mutants was also confirmed using another DCV marker, the insulin-like neuropeptide INS-22-YFP.

Figure S3: High-pressure freeze electron microscopic (HPF-EM) analysis showed normal DCV numbers at axonal release sites with a similar distribution and morphology compared with wild type. This indicates that Rab10 mutants do not affect the number of DCV but rather the secretion process.

Figure S4: To demonstrate that the results derived from Figure 1 aren't due to disruption in coelomocyte function, rab-10 mutants were analyzed for the coelomocyte uptake of soluble Texas Red-conjugated BSA (TR-BSA) injected into the body cavity. Neither uptake nor the kinetics of endocytosis was affected in rab-10 mutants.

Figure S5 D-F: In order to check if the defect in DCV exocytosis was cell-autonomous, tissue-specific knockdown of rab-10 by RNAi phenocopied the defect in NLP-21-YFP secretion with decreased YFP levels in coelomocytes.
Furthermore, Transgenic lines expressing mCherry-Rab-10 exclusively in the DA/DB motoneurons rescued the DCV secretion defect in rab-10 mutants (Figure 1C-E).

20/01/2021 Dnyanada:
Information on the species of the Rab10 cDNA used for generating genetic lines could not be retrieved. Hence, P91857 was chosen.

comments.rationale:
This paper introduces a new technique to measure DCV exocytosis kinetics using high-resolution membrane capacitance (Cm) combined with Ca2+ uncaging stimuli.

Figure 2A: Average Cm responses (bottom) induced by similar [Ca2+]i elevations (top) in wild-type (black trace), unc-31 mutant (red trace), unc-64 mutant (blue trace), and unc-18 mutant (grey trace) cells are compared. The inset compares the amplitude of burst exocytosis between wild-type, unc-31, unc-64, unc-18, and tag-81 mutant cells. The exocytotic burst is quantified as the amplitude of the exponential fit to the Cm trace.
Drastic reduction (~85%) in the amplitude of burst exocytosis of the Unc18 mutant indicates its role in DCV exocytosis.

Figure 7A: Density of near-membrane DCVs per unit area was slightly smaller in unc-18(e81) neurons.
Figure 7B: The average docking rate per unit area per minute was considerably reduced (by ~58%) in unc-18(e81) mutant cells.
Figure 7C: Docking events in the absence of UNC-18 were in general much shorter than those from wild-type cells.

Together, the data suggest that Unc18 plays a key role in presynaptic DCV exocytosis.

comments.species:
The catalytic arginine finger of TBC-4 was mutated to alanine to generate tbc-4 R155A. Wild-type tbc-4, tbc-4 (377-825), and the aforementioned tbc-4 R155A mutant were cloned into pGADT7 as prey. The tested plasmids were mixed to a final concentration of 100 ng/μL along with pbluescript. These mixtures were microinjected into C. elegans to generate transgenic lines as described previously (PMID: 20364145).
The tbc-4 (ok2928) and tbc-4(tm3255) were as TBC mutant-strains in the study. The corresponding worm gene is WBGene00020770 (eat-17).
comments.rationale:
Figure 1A: DCV secretion from cholinergic motoneurons was assayed using a transgenic strain (nuIs183) expressing the proneuropeptide NLP-21 tagged to YFP exclusively in dorsally projecting cholinergic motoneurons. This strain has been successfully used to assay DCV biogenesis and release. At the trans-Golgi, the proneuropeptide NLP-21-YFP fusion is packaged into DCVs, where it is subsequently processed into active neuropeptides and soluble YFP. YFP-labeled DCVs are then transported to axonal release sites. After fusion, the soluble YFP is released into the body cavity. Here, it is constitutively endocytosed by macrophage-like cells, called coelomocytes. The YFP fluorescence in coelomocytes can, therefore, be used as an indirect readout for DCV release.

Figure 3A: the coelomocyte YFP intensities were almost abolished in the two tbc-4 deletion alleles, tbc-4 (ok2928) and tbc-4 (tm3255), by 94.64 ± 2.10% and 95.82 ± 1.39%, respectively. Neuron-specific expression of tbc-4 in tbc-4 (ok2928) strain restored DCV exocytosis. Catalytically inactive TBC-4 R155A were unable to restore DCV exocytosis.

Figure 3F: TBC-4 colocalises with Rab-10 in VNC neurons. The paper proposes that tbc-4 might be responsible for regulating the function of Rab10 in DCV exocytosis.

20/01/2021 Dnyanada: The paper shows that Rab10 is involved in dense-core vesicle exocytosis, it also demonstrates that TBC4 is a putative GAP for Rab10. The term "regulation of ..." was chosen as TBC4 regulates dense-core vesicle exocytosis via its GAP activity on Rab10.

comments.rationale:
Figure 1A: DCV secretion from cholinergic motoneurons was assayed using a transgenic strain (nuIs183) expressing the proneuropeptide NLP-21 tagged to YFP exclusively in dorsally projecting cholinergic motoneurons. This strain has been successfully used to assay DCV biogenesis and release. At the trans-Golgi, the proneuropeptide NLP-21-YFP fusion is packaged into DCVs, where it is subsequently processed into active neuropeptides and soluble YFP. YFP-labeled DCVs are then transported to axonal release sites. After fusion, the soluble YFP is released into the body cavity. Here, it is constitutively endocytosed by macrophage-like cells, called coelomocytes. The YFP fluorescence in coelomocytes can, therefore, be used as an indirect readout for DCV release.

Figure 3A: Both an early-stop allele, tbc-2 (qx20), and a deletion allele, tbc-2 (tm2241), had reductions in coelomocyte YFP intensities by 71.36 ± 14.10% and 81.01 ± 4.00%, respectively. TBC-2 is known to be a RAB-5-specific GAP (PMID: 20462958) suggesting that TBC-2 might be regulating the function of Rab-5 in DCV exocytosis.

20/01/2021 Dnyanada:
Information on the species of the TBC2 cDNA used for generating genetic lines could not be retrieved. Hence, Q23419 was chosen.

comments.species: Conditional and constitutive knock-in mice were generated by Ozgene PLC (Australia) using a gene targeting approach in C57Bl/6 embryo stem cells (Bruce4). Genetic engineering targeted the Vps35 locus on murine chromosome 8 (85,260,392-85,299,802 reverse strand (GRCm38.p5); Ensemble genomic reference sequence ENSMUSG00000031696; NCBI mRNA reference sequence NM_022997.4). A floxed "mini-gene" consisting of: (1) splice acceptor, Vps35 exon 15-17 coding sequence, a polyadenylation signal (pA), and; (2) a PGK-neomycin (neo)-pA selection cassette internally flanked by FRT sites, was inserted into intron 14. The 5' targeting arm spanning endogenous exon 15 was used to introduce the Vps35 g.85,263,520G>A (p.D620N) mutation. Conditional animals (denoted cVKI) have their endogenous gene (exons 1-14) spliced to the mini-gene cassette (exons 15-17, pA); the PGK-neo-pA selection cassette was removed by crossing to transgenic animals expressing FlpE-recombinase. Heterozygous cVKI mice were crossed to transgenic animals expressing Cre-recombinase to remove the floxed mini-gene cassette, enabling heterozygous constitutive Vps35 p.D620N expression.
comments.rationale:
Fig a-c: Fast scan cyclic voltammetry indicates elevated dopamine release in VKI slices (VPS35 KI slices) compared to WT.
Fig 4f: Bathing slices with Quinpirole (a D2 agonist), shows enhanced inhibition of dopamine release in VKI slices when compared to WT.
Fig4d: Decay times for the evoked dopamine transients is slower in VKI slices than WT, suggesting slower re-uptake of extracellular dopamine.
Fig6: Western Blot analysis from striatum shows reduced total DAT protein levels and higher VMAT2 levels in VKI mice compared to WT. The enhanced dopamine evoked response can be correlated to elevated VMAT2 levels; while the increased decay time of dopamine release can be correlated to reduced DAT protein levels.

Based on the results above, one might infer deficits in activity-dependent transporter recycling (DAT) to the plasma membrane via VPS35-positive endosomes in VKI mice.

18/01/2021 Dnyanada: The general term "modulation of chemical synaptic transmission" was used due to limited synaptic evidence. However, it is an interesting paper that demonstrates the functional role of VPS35 in dopaminergic neurons.

comments.species: Snx27+/+, Snx27+/- and Snx27-/- mice were generated by crossing heterozygotes on C57BL/6 and 129/SV mixed backgrounds to produce F1 hybrid background mice. Cell surface biotinylation experiments were conducted in HEK cells.
comments.rationale:

Fig2i: LTP induced by high-frequency trains (100 Hz for 1 s) was significantly reduced in Snx27+/- mice compared to controls.
Both these results suggest that Snx27+/-might affect both AMPAR- and NMDAR-dependent synaptic events.
Fig 3a: Western blot analysis shows that Snx27+/- mice had lower amounts of GluR1, GluR2, NR1, NR2A and NR2B in both synaptosomal membranes and PSD fractions compared to Snx27+/+ littermates.
Fig 4d-f: Cell surface biotinylation experiments show that overexpression of SNX27 resulted in increased cell surface amounts of GluR1 and NR1 in GluR1-HEK293 and NR1-NR2A-HEK293 cells. Conversely, knockdown of SNX27 resulted in reduced cell surface expression of GluR1 and NR1. This effect was also evident in primary neurons; with a decrease in cell surface expression of GluR1 and NR1 in primary neurons derived from Snx27+/- mice.
Fig 4g-h: Receptor recycling assay shows that overexpression of SNX27 decreased the amount of internalized biotinylated GluR1 in GluR1-HEK293 cells. Consistent with these overexpression experiments, biotin-labelled GluR1 after treatment with SNX27 siRNA showed increased internalized biotinylated GluR1as compared to control siRNA.
Supplementary Fig 7: SNX27 does not influence endocytosis of GluR1.

comments.rationale:

The amplitude and decay times of mEPSC were unchanged indicating that the KO perhaps does not grossly affect transmitter quanta and receptors properties.
Fig 4G-H: In order to check if the reduced mEPSC frequency was due to altered synapse density in brain tissue, quantitative electron microscopy was performed. The number of excitatory synapses, the area density of synaptic vesicles, length of synaptic zones, the width of synaptic clefts and the area of synaptic terminals were not altered between Nrxn2A KO and WT suggesting that the differences observed in spontaneous excitatory transmission are not caused by structural defects.
Fig 5A-D: To evaluate if the reduction in mEPSC frequency is caused due to presynaptic mechanisms, paired-pulse facilitation paradigm was conducted. PPF was significantly reduced at most intervals in Nrxn2A-KO neurons.
Fig 5G-H: Quantitative analysis of NMDA/AMPA ratios revealed an almost 25% reduction in Nrxn2α KO neurons as compared to WT.

comments.species: The precise deletion of the pallidin locus was generated using flippase (FLP) recombinase-mediated recombination between pairs of transposon-based FRT sites, as described in the DrosDel Collection (Parks et al., 2004). Specifically, two transposons flanking the pallidin locus, pBacf05716 and pBacf05753 (Thibault et al., 2004), were obtained from the Bloomington Drosophila Stock Center. Each contained flippase recombination target (FRT) sites in the correct orientation to permit a precise deletion. Following FLP-mediated recombination and excision of the remaining hybrid transposon, we confirmed the deletion by PCR using the following primers: forward primer 5'-GTCATTGGGTGCAAAGTGCTC; reverse primer 5'-CTCCCGAGCTGCATGTTGAATC. This revealed that bases 11,689,565 to 11,691,527 on chromosome 3L were deleted. We named this mutant allele pldnΔ1. The transcript of the gene located 5' to pallidin is not perturbed, while an estimated 591 bases of the 3'UTR of sugb, the gene located 3' to the pldn locus, is deleted in pldnΔ1. This region overlaps with the predicted pallidin 3'UTR, making it difficult to conclude whether the neighboring gene is impacted.
comments.rationale:
Fig 6A: Under conditions of high extracellular calcium, NMJs were stimulated at 10 Hz for 10 min to deplete the synaptic vesicle pool, then recovery of the pool was measured for an additional 10 min, taking a test pulse every 5 s. Following an initial rapid depletion typically observed in the initial seconds of stimulation, wild-type synapses largely maintained synaptic vesicle release for the duration of the stimulus, ending at ~80% of the starting EPSP amplitude and rapidly recovering to above 90% of prestimulus amplitudes. In contrast, the stimulation protocol revealed a more rapid rundown of the synaptic vesicle pool in pldn mutants, ending at ~45% of the starting EPSP amplitude. pldn mutants failed to fully replenish the depleted synaptic vesicle pool over the course of the next 10 min of recovery following high-frequency stimulation, only recovering to ~60% of prestimulus amplitudes. This level of depletion was significantly reduced when a pldn transgene was expressed in motorneurons in a pldn mutant background.
This indicated that pallidin is required presynaptically to maintain the rapidly recycling synaptic vesicle pool.
Given the role of Pallidin in vesicle biogenesis ((Di Pietro et al., 2006; Delevoye et al., 2016), the paper explores the possibility that Pallidin might simply be effecting the initial vesicle pool without necessitating any additional role in synaptic vesicle recycling. To test this, shi mutants that disrupt temperature-dependent SV endocytosis were used.
Fig 6D: In shi mutants alone, full depletion of the entire synaptic vesicle pool was achieved after ~400 s of stimulation at 15 Hz in 2 mM extracellular calcium. Shi;pldn double mutant showed similar rates of depletion of the releasable synaptic vesicle pool.
Fig 6E: Upon quantification of total quanta released in each mutant until full depletion, no significant differences between the genotypes were observed.

From this, one can infer that pldn is not required for the biogenesis or establishment of a full initial synaptic vesicle pool size, but rather is necessary to rapidly replenish depleted synaptic vesicles during and following high levels of activity.

comments.species: The w1118 strain was used as the wild-type control and blos1ex2 (Cheli et al., 2010) was used as Blos1 KO.
comments.rationale:
Fig3A-D: Blos1 contributes to the stability of pallidin in NMJ.

Fig 6B: Under conditions of high extracellular calcium, NMJs were stimulated at 10 Hz for 10 min to deplete the synaptic vesicle pool, then recovery of the pool was measured for an additional 10 min, taking a test pulse every 5 s. Following an initial rapid depletion typically observed in the initial seconds of stimulation, wild-type synapses largely maintained synaptic vesicle release for the duration of the stimulus, ending at ~80% of the starting EPSP amplitude and rapidly recovering to above 90% of prestimulus amplitudes. In contrast, the stimulation protocol revealed a more rapid rundown of the synaptic vesicle pool in Blos1 mutants, Blos1 mutants failed to fully replenish the depleted synaptic vesicle pool over the course of the next 10 min of recovery following high-frequency stimulation. This indicated that Blos1 might be required presynaptically to maintain the rapidly recycling synaptic vesicle pool.

From this, one can infer that Blos1 is involved in replenishing depleted synaptic vesicles during and following high levels of activity.

comments.species: Frozen adult Sprague Dawley rat brains were custom collected by Rockland Immunochemicals Inc. (Gilbertsville, PA) for subcellular localization studies.
comments.rationale:
Fig 3: Subcellular fractions were obtained from adult rat cerebral cortex and the distribution of FAM81A protein was monitored using two antibodies (top two panels). FAM81A immunopositive band at ~42 kDa was found to be highly enriched in the PSD fraction, in parallel with PSD-95, whereas the nuclear fraction showed very little labelling at that position with either Ab1 or Ab2. Other bands in the nuclear fraction that were immunopositive with both Ab1 and Ab2 were further analyzed by mass spectrometry, but no peptides corresponding to FAM81A were identified (data not shown).
Fig 4: Immuno-electron microscopy on excitatory synapses from adult mice hippocampus (Fig 4A-C) and cerebral cortex (Fig D-E) showed specific labelling of FAM81A protein in the postsynaptic density.
Fig 5: Laminar distribution of FAM81A label was concentrated at the cytoplasmic edge of the PSD core, with a mean distance of 34.1±1.1 nm from the postsynaptic membrane in the hippocampus and 32.6±1.1 nm from the postsynaptic membrane in the cerebral cortex.
Supplementary Fig 3: Immunoreaction distribution profile in laminar layers of PSD of FAM81A was compared with that of PSD95, GKAP and Homer. FAM81A labelling follows the same pattern of distribution as GKAP, while PSD95 and Homer show distribution in the PSD core and PSD pallium.

Fig4, Fig5 and Fig S3, the authors claim that FAM81A is majorly concentrated at the cytoplasmic core of PSD. Uniprot does not show any transmembrane domains for this protein (nor for its perhaps better annotated human ortholog). Based on this, the SynGO term "postsynaptic density, intracellular component" was used.

The authors do not comment on the specificity of the FAM81A antibody.

comments.species: Primary cultures of hippocampal neurons were prepared from C57Bl/6 mouse fetuses at gestational day 18 as previously described (Nyman-Huttunen et al., 2006).
comments.rationale:
In order to test the function of ICAM5 in synapse assembly; synapsin I and PSD-95 were used as markers for pre- and post-synapses respectively, and the colocalization of the two markers were used to evaluate the level of the pre- and post-synaptic contacts.
Fig 1A-B: At 15 day in vitro (DIV), in ICAM-5-/- neurons, synapsin I puncta accumulated on the spine heads while in WT neurons, they scatter along the dendritic shafts. The overlap between synapsin I and PSD-95 was significantly increased in ICAM-5-/- (78%±3%) neurons compared with WT (51%±5%) and the colocalization mainly increased in spine heads.

To study whether the increased synaptic contacts in ICAM-5-/- neurons are functionally active, the inter-event intervals and amplitude of miniature excitatory postsynaptic currents (mEPSCs) in cultured WT and ICAM-5-deficient neurons were recorded.
Fig 1C-E: Compared with WT, ICAM-5-/- neurons exhibited a significant increase in the frequency (decrease in the inter-event intervals) of mEPSCs, however, there was no significant effect on the amplitude. The mean relative inter-event interval was 53±11% shorter in ICAM-5-/- than in WT neurons implying a significant increase in the frequency of mEPSC.

18/01/2021: The term "regulation of synapse assembly" was chosen instead of "regulation of synapse maturation" as the paper demonstrates the role of ICAM5 in fully mature synapse.

comments.species: The long transcript splice-variant of human NHE6 (NHE6v1; NCBI refseq NM_001042537) was cloned from a human brain Matchmaker cDNA library (Clontech) using PCR methodology and was engineered to contain the influenza virus hemagglutinin (HA) (YPYDVPDYAS) epitope at its extreme C-terminal end. This construct was termed wild-type NHE6-HA (NHE6WT-HA) and inserted into the HindIII and XbaI sites of the mammalian expression vector pcDNA3 (Invitrogen), as described previously (Ilie et al., 2014). NHE6-HA was then used as a template to engineer the double deletion mutation of amino acids E287 and S288 (ΔE287/S288, ΔES) by PCR mutagenesis. mCherry fluorescent protein (mCh) C-terminal-tagged forms of NHE6 WT and ΔES mutant were constructed by insertion between the XhoI and HindIII restriction sites of the pAcGFP1-N1 vector (BD Biosciences Clontech, Palo Alto, CA). The In vitro experiments were performed on primary hippocampal cultures prepared from early postnatal C57BL/6 mice.
comments.rationale:
Fig 4A-C & TableS5: Endogenous WT NHE6 colocalizes strongly with the GluA1 subunit of AMPARs. However, this overlap is significantly attenuated in neurons expressing NHE6ΔES-mCh (SLC9A6 KO) and is accompanied by a significant decrease in GluA1 puncta at spines, indicating that the ΔES mutant deters the trafficking of GluA1 to excitatory synapses.
Fig 4D-E: To investigate if the decrease in GluA1 levels in NHE6ΔES mutant is due to enhanced trafficking of GluA1 receptors to lysosomes, neurons were co-transfected with EGFP and influenza virus hemagglutinin (HA)-tagged constructs of NHE6 WT or ΔES to allow for double immunolabeling of the lysosomal marker LAMP1 and GluA1. Interestingly, in NHE6ΔES-HA-expressing cells, there was greater colocalization between LAMP1 and GluA1 compared to neurons expressing NHE6WT-HA. This finding implies that NHE6ΔES mutant preferentially targets GluA1 to lysosomal compartments rather than recycling endosomes.

To investigate if NHE6ΔES mutant's role in AMPAR trafficking has an effect on glycine-mediated LTP, neurons were cotransfected with tdTomato (tdT) and N-terminal fused pH-sensitive superecliptic pHluorin (SEP)-GluA1 (sGluA1) alone, or with HA-tagged NHE6 WT or ΔES. Then they were subjected to a glycine-mediated chemical LTP (gly-ChemLTP) protocol to emulate NMDA receptor (NMDAR)-dependent LTP induction at Schaffer collateral-CA1 synapses in the hippocampus.
Fig5A-C: 20 minutes following gly-ChemLTP induction in tdT control- and NHE6WT-HA-transfected neurons, a significant increase in the number of spines containing sGluA1 and upregulation of their puncta in the heads of these spines compared to unstimulated sister control cultures was observed. In contrast, gly-ChemLTP stimulation in NHE6ΔES-HA-expressing neurons did not show an increase in sGluA1 localization at spines or within the spine head compared to unstimulated controls.

Fig4A-C: SynaptopHluorin, a VAMP-2/synaptobrevin-2 fused with a pH-sensitive variant of GFP was used to check if the interaction between snx9 and dynamin1 could be involved in SV endocytosis. The fluorescence of spH is quenched once synaptic vesicles are endocytosed and re-acidified (from external pH ~7.4 to an internal pH of a synaptic vesicle ~5.5) and reliably reflects the kinetics of endocytosis. To investigate the effect of SNX9 on endocytosis, FLAG-tagged SNX9 or truncated SNX9 variants were cotransfected with spH into hippocampal neurons. Upon electrical stimulation (600 actions potentials/20 Hz), the fluorescence intensity of individual spH boutons increased rapidly, reached a peak, and then decayed with an exponential time course. In boutons expressing SNX9, synaptic vesicle endocytosis occurred much more slowly than in non-expressing boutons.
Fig 4D: Histograms of the rates of spH fluorescence decay demonstrate that SNX9 overexpression significantly slows SV endocytosis than control.
Fig 5A: An alternative method of measuring SV endocytosis involved employing FM 4-64, a red-shifting fluorescent lipophilic dye with the same protocol as in for Fig4.
Fig 5B-C: The intensity of FM 4-64 staining of SNX9- or SNX9-SH3-transfected synaptic boutons were invariably higher than that of the control boutons confirming that endocytosis proceeds more slowly when SNX9 was overexpressed.
Fig 8D-E: Co-transfecting neurons with Snx9 siRNA constructs and spH demonstrated a similar slowing of SV endocytosis.
Fig 8A-C: The efficiency of Snx9 SiRNA constructs was verified by staining with the anti-snx9 antibody. The expression of snx9 was significantly lowered in neurons transfected with siRNA constructs than control. The expression of other endocytic proteins such as syndapin, dynamin, endophilin, and Rab5b was not affected.

The authors claim that overexpression of SNX9 may act in a dominant-negative manner to prevent dynamin or N-WASP from interacting with other endocytic proteins. While silencing the expression of SNX9 could affect its physiological role in endocytosis. Overall, Snx9 seems to impair SV endocytosis in neurons.

Fig5: Recombinant homomeric AMPA receptor subunit (GluR2 R586Q) was expressed in organotypic hippocampal slices. The mutation R586Q at the channel pore prevents the receptor from conducting outward currents at positive membrane potentials (inward rectification). The synaptic delivery of the recombinant receptor can be detected as an increase in the ratio of the AMPA receptor-mediated response at -60 mV versus the response at +40 mV (rectification index). In the absence of radicicol, expression of the recombinant receptor produced inward rectification (increase in the rectification index) compared to control indicating the delivery of the homomeric receptor. Thirty-minute incubation with radicicol on slices expressing GluR2 (R586Q) blocked this rectification because GluR2 receptors might be constitutively cycling in and out of synapses. This suggests the probable role of hsp90 for either the synaptic reinsertion of AMPA receptors during their continuous cycling or their stability once inserted at synapses.

Fig2: Endogenous SNX4 colocalizes with early and recycling endosomal markers RAB5 (Pearson's coefficient 0.58) and Rab11 (Pearson's coefficient 0.45) in mouse hippocampal neurons. FigS3A-B: The localization of endogenous SNX4 to the presynapse was also observed using bassoon, a marker of the presynaptic active zone.

Fig4A-E: Subcellular fractions of the mouse hippocampus detected SNX4 in the synaptosome (SyS) and synaptic membrane fraction (SyM) comparable to the expression profiles of presynaptic marker Vamp2.

Fig4F-G: Immuno-gold electron microscopy localised SNX4 inside the presynaptic terminals (as marked by 'T'). Quantitative analysis shows that the SNX4 immunosignal was more abundant in the presynaptic than the postsynaptic terminal.
FigS4: The findings of the immunogold EM were verified by a reduction in signal when SNX4 antibody was incubated with blocking peptide (Synaptic Systems, Cat. No. 392-0P at a ratio of 1:10).

The specificity of the SNX4 antibody was verified via Western blot and immunocytochemistry along with the SNX4 knockdowns.
Fig1A-B: Western blot showed an expected SNX4 band of ~50kD band. Inclusion of SNX4 knockdowns showed a reduction in signal intensity which was rescued upon inclusion of their corresponding rescue constructs.

Fig1B-F: Immunocytochemistry also showed that the total SNX4 signal intensity was decreased upon SNX4 knockdown and was restored when shRNAs were combined with their rescue constructs. On the other hand, the total synaptophysin-1 intensity remained unchanged upon modulation of SNX4 levels.

20/01/2021 Dnyanada:
The paper shows that p75NTR KO leads to a reduction in the number of SV/AZ/RRPs, however, simply based on ultrastructural data, it is difficult to attribute the consequence of this on synaptic BP. Hence, a generic term "presynaptic modulation of chemical synaptic transmission" was chosen.

comments.rationale:
Loss of RBP1,2 in double knockout mice show impaired presynaptic localization of BKα-channel protein (Figure 8). Presynaptic BK channels act as negative regulators of neurotransmitter release by hyperpolarizing the plasma membrane in response to AP-stimulated depolarization and Ca2+ entry through CaV channels. They show also that BK currents (amplitude and density) are abolished in the RBP1,2 double knockout mice (Figure 7). Therefore, RIM-binding proteins 1 & 2 control potassium currents and membrane potential presynaptically.

18/01/2021 Dnyanada: BK are large-conductance calcium-activated potassium channels that are enriched in the presynapse (Robitaille et al, 1993a; Knaus et al, 1996; Zhou et al, 1999; Hu et al, 2001; Ishikawa et al, 2003; Misonou et al, 2006; Nakamura & Takahashi, 2007). The current paper shows that deletion of RBP decreases and decelerates presynaptic BK currents (Figure 5, 6) by impairing presynaptic localisation of BK channels (Figure 8; as described in the annotation). Based on this, the ontology term "regulation of presynaptic membrane potential" was chosen.
Note: FigS2C uses IP to demonstrate that RIMBP1,2 dKO does not alter the levels of BK channels as compared to WT. However, it is interesting to note that RIMBP1,2dKO samples stained against anti-RIMBP2 show a light band which means that RIMBP1,2 dKO model might not be completely abrogating the expression of RIMBP2.

18/01/2021 Dnyanada: CtBP1 occurs in nuclear and cytoplasmic pools of the brain and cultured neurons and is suggested to be shuttling between the nucleus and cytoplasm (PMID:25652077). The current paper demonstrates its dynamic interaction with Dynamin1, a key player of the endocytic machinery. Based on this, the term "extrinsic component of presynaptic endocytic zone membrane" was chosen.

Cd2apKO mouse used previously in PMID: 10514378
Mice lacking CD2AP were generated by replacing the exon encoding the first SRC homology 3 (SH3) domain of CD2AP with a neomycin resistance gene. Homozygous CD2AP knockout (KO) mice were generated from heterozygous mice with a normal frequency of 25%.
comments.rationale:
"CA2AP plays a role in Synaptic Proteostasis"
Firstly, in this study, the authors carried out experiments with Cindr gene (fly homolog of the Alzheimer's risk gene CD2AP) and they observed that:

Cindr is required for synaptic maturation (high lethality in cindr homozygotes phenotypes). They demonstrated an incomplete boutons differentiation in mutant phenotypes of cindr (Figs 2D, 2F, S2D and S3B), less active zones (Fig S6E) and abnormal synaptic terminals elongation (Fig S6B and S6E); also less synaptic vesicle endocytosis. But mainly, they observed that the loss of cindr provokes increases of Synapsin and PMCA proteins (Figs 5A and 5B) and a reduction of 14-3-3zheta protein, all related to defects in proteasome function.

After they observed in (Figures 7A and 7B) elevations in the synaptic proteins Synapsin-1 and Synaptophysin, also of an increase of PMCA or reduction of 14-3-3 protein levels in brain homogenates prepared from 5-month-old Cd2ap null animals, like previously for Drosophila findings. Also, in Fig 7C they confirmed the reduction of ubiquitin-proteasome system activity in Cd2ap null mice, through in vitro proteasome assay.

In conclusion, they hypothesize that CD2AP/Cindr regulate/play a role in synaptic proteostasis.

20/01/2021 Dnyanada: The annotation uses both drosophila and mouse biological systems, CD2AP_MOUSE was used as the Uniprot identifier for this annotation.

comments.species: Mutant Lphn3 conditional mice containing an N-terminal double HA tag were generated by introducing the tag into the coding region of the 3' exon following the exon with the start codon and the sequence encoding for the signal peptide.
comments.rationale:
By using conditional Lphn3 KO mice, the authors sparsely express Cre to compare Lphn3 KO primary neurons to adjacent wild type neurons in culture. Loss of Lphn3 leads to a reduction in excitatory postsynaptic density in excitatory synapses (Fig 1D) and not in inhibitory synapses (Fig 1E). This can be rescued by re-expressing Lphn3 but not by re-expressing mutants that block binding of FLRT (4A mutation) or teneurin (ΔLEC mutation) (Fig 4C), known presynaptic partners of Lphn3.

This results are confirmed in intact tissue by analyzing spine density in hippocampal neurons sparsely transduced with Cre-GFP virus and filled with biocytin. This reveals that Lphn3 only controls spine density in 2 of the 3 major synaptic hippocampal layers (S. oriens and S. radiatum but not in S. lacunosum-moleculare).

In addition, to demonstrate that Lphn3 is a potent inducer of presynaptic excitatory specializations into regions expressing Lphn3, authors use cocultured neurons and HEK cells in an artificial synapse formation assay. HEK cells expressing GFP and Lphn3 show strong vGlut staining, indicating that presynaptic terminals of cultured neurons can synapse into HEK cells that express Lphn3. Control with only GFP expression does not induce any vGlut staining at the HEK cell surface (Fig S9A, S9C).

Skywalker (Sky) facilitates endosomal trafficking of synaptic vesicles at Drosophila neuromuscular junction boutons"
comments.rationale:
To study the protein expression pattern and subcellular localization of TBC1D24 / Skywalker (short name Sky), authors created a genomic EGFP-tagged construct (GFP-Sky+) (Figure S1E). The presence of this construct rescues sky related phenotypes (Figure 1C), indicating that GFP-Sky is functional. GFP-Sky appears enriched at synaptic areas in the ventral nerve cord (VNC) of third instar larvae (L3) (Figure 1E). Authors also observe abundant labeling at neuromuscular junction (NMJ) boutons where Sky is present both pre- and postsynaptically (Figure 1H-M). Additionally, an antibody raised against full length HIS-Sky also labels the VNC neuropile (Figure 1F) and NMJ boutons, and this staining is strongly reduced in sky hypomorphic mutants (more than 2-fold), indicating the labeling is specific (Figure 1G).

Rationale for cytosolic localization is inferred from protein properties, as it does not present any transmembrane domains.

14/01/2021 Dnyanada: The paper demonstrates the localisation of GFP-TBC1D24 in the NMJ. However, the images do not provide sufficient resolution to distinguish between pre or postsynaptic localisation. Besides, the localisation is based on overexpression of the protein. Based on these two points, "synapse" was chosen as the appropriate ontology term.

comments.species: "Larvae were grown on grape juice plates with fresh yeast paste", "All fly stocks were kept on standard corn meal and molasses medium at room temperature", "In this work, we present evidence that (...) Skywalker (Sky) facilitates endosomal trafficking of synaptic vesicles at Drosophila neuromuscular junction boutons"
comments.rationale:
Figure 6. The authors find that neurotransmitter release and the readily releasable pool are increased in TBC1D24 / Skywalker mutants in drosophila. To show that TBC1D24 / Skywalker mutations affect neurotransmitter release, authors recorded excitatory junctional potentials (EJPs) elicited at 1 Hz. EJP amplitudes are increased in mutants when compared to controls over a range of Ca2+ concentrations (0.3-1 mM), but saturate above 2 mM Ca2+ (Figures 6A and 6B). Authors also find that this increased neurotransmission in sky mutants does not result in quicker synaptic depression during trains of repetitive stimulation (Figure S5). Hence, sky mutations result in increased transmitter release but harbour a normal calcium dependence of release. In addition, activity-driven Ca2+ increases are also confirmed to not be altered in Skywalker mutants using calcium imaging with the optical sensor G-CaMP1.6.

To estimate junctional quantal content authors measured EJCs in voltage clamp. In Skywalker mutants, EJCs recorded in 0.5 mM Ca2+ are increased and this is rescued in larvae expressing wild-type Skywalker (Figures 6C and 6D). Consequently, the authors conclude the quantal content (EJC/mEJC) to be nearly doubled in sky mutants compared controls (Figure 6E).

18/01/2021 Dnyanada: The paper establishes that Sky (TBC1D24) is a GTPase activating protein specific for Rab35 (Figure 5). Expression of a dominant-negative version of Rab35 in sky mutants restores FM1-43 to a wildtype like distribution, indicating that Skywalker functions to regulate Rab35-mediated trafficking. Furthermore, ubiquitinated proteins (an artificial chimeric version of synaptobrevin) is more efficiently shuttled for degradation in sky mutants relative to WT (Figure 7).
The effect of sky on the synaptic vesicle cycle (as described in the annotation; Figure 6) can be attributed to its ability to regulate endosomal processing of synaptic vesicle proteins. Based on this, the ontology term "synaptic vesicle endosomal processing" was used for this annotation.
As the effect on SV endosomal processing in sky mutants is not drastically altered, the "regulation" box was ticked.

comments.rationale:
It is known that activation of opioid receptors leads to the activation of inwardly rectifying potassium channels and inhibition of voltage-gated calcium channels, leading to a decrease in neurotransmitter release (reviewed in PMID: 30301203).

Figure 1. In this work the authors show that Parvalbumin expressing (PV) neurons release GABA onto pyramidal cells, and this process is modulated by presynaptic μ opioid receptors (MORs). Activating PV cells using optogenetics, the authors identify GABAergic postsynaptic currents (dissected using pharmacology) and show that pharmacological activation of MORs (using DAMGO) leads to a decrease in GABA release into pyramidal cells (Figure 1B). This activation can be blocked by naloxone pretreatment (an MOR antagonist) to show the specificity of MOR activation (Figure 1C).

As it is known that MORs depress presynaptic release by modulating voltage-gated calcium channels, MOR is annotated for "presynaptic modulation of chemical synaptic transmission".

"Cindr is mainly expressed at the presynapse"

In Fig 1B, they demonstrate that Cindr appears enriched within the neuropil, colocalizating with the presynaptic marker Bruchpilot (nc82). This assay was carried out in adult brain, although the expression/localization of Cindr was observed also in larval state.

In Fig 1C, the authors show that Cindr is enriched within the synaptic terminal boutons at neuromuscular junctions, colocalizating with presynaptic markers but not with postsynaptic ones. For this assay, they used the larval peripheral nervous system.

In Fig 1D, Cindr presents a similar localization to other binding partners at the neuromuscular junction, like Synapsin or Synaptotagmin.

comments.species: This study generated Liprin-α3- KO mice by using CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing in single-cell zygotes. An allele was selected that had an 8-bp deletion (Fig. 2A), inducing a frame-shift mutation leading to nonsense-mediated decay. Heterozygote matings produced offsprings with a Mendelian distribution of homozygote KO (Liprin-α3-/-), heterozygote (Liprin-α3+/-), and WT (Liprin-α3+/+) sibling mice (Fig. 2B). Western blotting of brain homogenates revealed that Liprin-α3 was removed, and bands that would establish the presence of protein fragment were not detected (Fig. 2C). Liprin-α3-/- mice were viable and fertile, but had a significantly increased distance traveled and were less spatially confined in an open-field assessment of locomotion (Fig. S3 A-D), suggesting alterations in brain function. No changes beyond removal of Liprin-α3 were detected when we assessed morphology and protein composition in hippocampi of Liprin-α3-/- mice (Fig. S3 E-H). Primary mouse hippocampal cultures were generated from newborns and all analyses were performed at DIV 14-17. Stimulated emission depletion (STED) superresolution microscopy was used to demonstrate liprin alpha 3 localization at the AZ.
comments.rationale:
Cultured hippocampal neurons stained with antibodies against the synaptic vesicle markers - vGlut or synapsin, the active zone protein -Bassoon, and liprin alpha 3 were imaged using STED microscopy and pairwise stainings of synapses in side view were analyzed for all known AZ proteins and liprin alpha 3. To assess the localization of each protein within and outside the active zone, two masks were generated (Fig. 1A): one that outlined the nerve terminal (vGlut1 or Synapsin; Fig. 1A, blue), and one that defined the active zone (BassoonN; Fig. 1A, green). The area associated with the active zone for each protein was quantified (Fig. 1A, yellow) and compared with the area of the same protein outside the active zone (Fig. 1A, red), normalized to the sum of the area of active zone and nonactive zone components (Fig. 1E). This provides a measure of signal distribution within a nerve terminal without accounting for the signal intensity within the area. For Bassoon, RIM1, ELKS2, RIM-BP2, and Munc13-1, the majority of the area stained for was at the active zone (73-90%; Fig. 1E). For Liprin-α3, ~50% of the positively stained area was outside the active zone but the peak intensity was within the active zone.

comments.rationale:
Figure 3A-D: The mEJC amplitudes in both dor35 and dor36 mutants (orange) were larger compared with controls and were rescued by restoring the expression of Dor ubiquitously (daGAL4; green).
Figure 3F: The quantal content (EJC/mEJC) in dor mutants is reduced compared with controls suggesting that in dor mutants, fewer vesicles fuse with the synaptic membrane upon nerve stimulation.
Figure S2B: Quantification of synaptic vesicle diameter using transmission EM (TEM) of dor35 and dor36 mutant synaptic boutons does not reveal a difference in mean synaptic vesicle size compared with controls indicating that the effect on mEJCs is not due to larger vesicles that harbour more neurotransmitters.

To test whether fewer vesicles fuse upon stimulation in dor mutants, FM 1-43 dye labelling of NMJ nerve terminal was done to trace new vesicles that are trafficked from plasma membrane.
Figure 3G-H: dor mutants internalize less dye and the effect was rescued by restoring the expression of Dor ubiquitously (GAL4 ; green) or presynaptically (vGlutGAL4; purple).
Figure S2B-D: Synaptic vesicle number, the presence of endocytic intermediates, and the number of vesicles tethered at presynaptic release sites were not different in dor mutants.
Figure 3I-J: RRP is ~30% smaller in dor mutants compared with controls suggesting the defect in quantal content observed in dor mutants may be attributed, at least in part, to a smaller RRP.

The paper demonstrates that dor (VPS18) plays a role in endosomal trafficking of synaptic vesicles. Due to a lack of such ontology term, the parent term "regulation of synaptic vesicle cycle" was used.

comments.rationale:
This paper shows that PTPRS deletion in excitatory neurons in the cortex and hippocampus by conditional KO approach leads to decreased NMDAR currents and NMDAR-dependent LTP in the postsynaptic side of excitatory synapses at hippocampal CA3-CA1 synapses, suggestive of trans-synaptic regulation of postsynaptic NMDAR function by a presynaptic adhesion molecule, although it does not seem to involve a direct transsynaptic interaction of PTPRS with its knwon postsynaptic adhesion partners such as HSPG/CSPG or Slitrk1/TrkC. Another supportive paper from Thomas Sudhof's group (see above) demonstrates that a triple deletion of PTPRS, PTPRD, and LAR (three known members of the LAR family of receptor tyrosine phosphatases) leads to decreased postsynaptic NMDAR currents, again supportive of transsynaptic mechanisms.

This annotation is part of a systematic annotation of all synaptic vesicle V-ATPases.

Rationale: The luminal V-ATPase is known to be present in the membrane of synaptic vesicles where it drives the import of neurotransmitter molecules via a range of antiporter protein complexes (PMID:28383767). The mammalian V-ATPases consists of a peripheral V1 domain and an integral V0 domain that together play a role in synaptic vesicle proton loading (PMID: 16524922, 32165585). The V1 domain is known to be involved in ATP hydrolysis while the V0 domain is known to be involved in proton translocation across the synaptic vesicle membrane. The annotated paper explores the role of V-ATPase in synaptic vesicle proton loading with regards to synaptic vesicle endo/exocytosis.

Figure 1B: V-ATPase tagged subunits expressed in hippocampal neurons shows a punctate fluorescent pattern and colocalises with presynaptic marker Synaptobrevin2-pHluorin (Syb2-pHl) indicating a localisation in presynaptic boutons.

Figure 4A and S4: Fluorescence recovery curves of GFP-V1B2 show a decrease in ampltidue in silence conditions (0 mM Ca2+, 1 mM TTX) compared to a depolarised condition (45 mM K+). Similar profiles were observed for subunits GFP-V1A and GFP-V1H. Upon lumenal pH neutralisation (NH4Cl) and alkalinization (FCCP) conditions, fluorescence recovery of GFP-V1B2 is almost completely abolished indicating a crucial role of intravesicular pH as a regulator of V-ATPase assembly at presynaptic boutons.

Figure 5A-C: A significant decrease in cumulative exocytosis amplitude is observed in the presence of SaliPhe (70% for V0c-pHl and 65% for Syb2-pHl) indicating that pharmocologically locking the assembly of V-ATPase leads to a decline in release.

Figure 7E: Schematic depicts the role of V-ATPase assembly/disassembly in NT uptake coupled to the SV exo/endocytosis cycle."

comments.species: Synaptosomes from rat brain were isolated as described in (Fischer von Mollard et al., 1991) and then were subjected to limited proteolysis to dissociate pre- and postsynaptic membranes (Fig1A). Presynaptic components including both active zone and synaptic vesicle proteins remained intact after limited proteolysis whereas cell adhesion molecules and plasma membrane resident neurotransmitter receptors were cleaved (Figure 1B). Protease-treated synaptosomes were lysed by osmotic shock to release their cytoplasmic constituents, including nondocked synaptic vesicles. The sample was then fractionated on a 0.4-1.4 M continuous sucrose gradient (Figure 3A). Purification of docked synaptic vesicles was carried out immunoisolation using nonporous microbeads covalently coated with antibodies against the synaptic vesicle protein synaptophysin (Fig 3B). These isolated docked synaptic vesicles were then subjected to tandem mass spectrometry combined with quantitative proteomics.
comments.rationale:
